definition_zh: n. 洪水；暴雨；大量涌来的事物 v. 淹没；使充斥；使应接不暇
definition_en: a great flood or heavy rain, or a huge amount of something arriving at once
core_image: 河水漫过堤岸，街道变成水道，邮箱里同时塞进上百封未读邮件
scene: 洪水冲毁了那座老桥。 The deluge destroyed the old bridge.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：deluge 指洪水；句意是洪水冲毁了那座老桥。

pos.zh: 洪水；暴雨；大量涌来的事物
淹没；使充斥；使应接不暇

senses.title: Great flood
senses.definition: a great flood of water covering land that is usually dry
senses.definitionCN: 淹没平时干燥土地的大水
senses.example: The deluge destroyed the old bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水冲毁了那座老桥。
senses.why: A river climbing over its own bank.
senses.whyCN: 一条爬过自己堤岸的河。

senses.title: Heavy rain
senses.definition: a very heavy fall of rain
senses.definitionCN: 极大的降雨
senses.example: We were caught in a deluge on the moor.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在荒地上遇上了暴雨。
senses.why: Rain falling faster than the gutters can take it.
senses.whyCN: 雨落得比排水沟能承受的更快。

senses.title: A flood of things
senses.definition: a huge amount of something arriving at the same time
senses.definitionCN: 大量事物同时涌来
senses.example: The office was deluged with complaints.
senses.exampleCN: 办公室被投诉淹没了。
senses.why: An inbox with a hundred unread lines.
senses.whyCN: 一个有一百条未读的收件箱。

intro.en: Deluge comes from Latin diluvium, a great flood, from diluere, to wash away.
intro.cn: deluge 源自拉丁语 diluvium（大洪水），后者来自 diluere（冲走）。

items.en: Luere meant to wash or wash away.
items.cn: luere 意为洗、冲走。

items.en: Diluere meant to wash away or dissolve.
items.cn: diluere 意为冲走、溶解。

items.en: Diluvium named a great flood.
items.cn: diluvium 指大洪水。

items.en: Deluge entered English through Old French for the biblical flood.
items.cn: 十四世纪 deluge 经古法语进入英语，指圣经中的大洪水。

items.en: It widened to any overwhelming downpour or rush.
items.cn: 十七世纪扩展到任何压倒性的暴雨或涌来。

items.en: It is now common for floods of mail and requests.
items.cn: 如今常用于邮件与请求的洪流。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the lu- washing and playing family; the near-meaning group names things that arrive in overwhelming amounts.
note.cn: 形近组共享 lu-（冲、戏）家族；近义组都是「量大到压倒」的说法。

entries.definition: To make someone believe something false.
entries.definitionCN: 欺骗；哄骗。

entries.definition: To make a liquid thinner or weaker.
entries.definitionCN: 稀释；冲淡。

entries.definition: To refer to something indirectly.
entries.definitionCN: 暗指；提及。

entries.definition: A large amount of water covering dry land.
entries.definitionCN: 洪水。

entries.definition: A fast, violent flow of water or rain.
entries.definitionCN: 急流；暴雨。

entries.definition: A very heavy fall of rain.
entries.definitionCN: 倾盆大雨。

entries.definition: A mass of snow sliding down, or a sudden huge amount.
entries.definitionCN: 雪崩；大量涌来。

normalIntro.en: Deluge is water washing everything away: a river, a storm, or a hundred emails at once.
normalIntro.cn: deluge 就是把一切冲走的水：一条河、一场暴雨，或一次涌来的一百封邮件。

normal.en: Lu- means to wash, as in dilute.
normal.cn: lu- 意为冲、洗，如 dilute。

normal.en: Diluvium was the Latin word for a great flood.
normal.cn: diluvium 是拉丁语的大洪水。

normal.en: A deluge covers land that is normally dry.
normal.cn: deluge 淹没平时干燥的土地。

normal.en: Be deluged with work means too much work at once.
normal.cn: be deluged with work 指工作一次涌来太多。

normal.en: A deluge of complaints fills the inbox.
normal.cn: 大量投诉塞满收件箱。

abstract.en: A river climbing over its own bank.
abstract.cn: 一条爬过自己堤岸的河。

abstract.en: Rain falling faster than the gutters can take it.
abstract.cn: 雨落得比排水沟能承受的更快。

abstract.en: An inbox with a hundred unread lines.
abstract.cn: 一个有一百条未读的收件箱。

examples.en: The village was deluged by the storm.
examples.cn: 村庄被暴风雨淹没了。

examples.en: A deluge of applications arrived on Monday.
examples.cn: 周一涌来大量申请。

examples.en: They deluged the minister with questions.
examples.cn: 他们向部长连珠炮似地提问。

dict_mnemonic.text: deluge 源自拉丁语 diluvium（大洪水），由 di-（离开）＋ luere（冲、洗）构成：水把一切冲走，就是「洪水、暴雨」；邮件把你冲走，就是「被淹没」。

root: 拉丁语 luere（冲、洗）→ diluere（冲走）→ diluvium（大洪水）→ 古法语 deluge → 英语 deluge

sensesIntro.en: One water rushing in: a river, a storm and an inbox.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一股冲进来的水：一条河、一场暴雨与一个收件箱。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a river climbing over its bank while an inbox fills with a hundred unread lines
core.cn: 核心意象：河水爬过堤岸，收件箱同时塞进一百条未读

branches.en: A river climbing over its own bank.
branches.cn: 一条爬过自己堤岸的河。

branches.en: Rain falling faster than the gutters can take it.
branches.cn: 雨落得比排水沟能承受的更快。

branches.en: An inbox with a hundred unread lines.
branches.cn: 一个有一百条未读的收件箱。

branches.en: Both are water arriving faster than it can drain.
branches.cn: 两者都是水来得比排得更快。

branches.en: Both overwhelm by sheer quantity at once.
branches.cn: 两者都以一次涌来的量压垮对方。

intro.en: Deluge is built on lu-, to wash; the same root builds dilute and the flood family.
intro.cn: deluge 建立在 lu-（冲、洗）之上；同一词根造出 dilute 与洪水一族词。

latinIntro.en: Latin luere means to wash, unda a wave and torrere to parch.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 luere 意为冲洗，unda 意为波浪，torrere 意为烤干。

definition_zh: 可分解的；可降解的；可拆解的
definition_en: capable of being broken down into simpler parts
core_image: 一只纸袋埋在土里，几个月后只剩纤维的痕迹
scene: 这里指「可分解的」。 The packaging is fully decomposable, so it can be buried with the food waste.
sceneCN: 这里 decomposable 是「可降解的」（第 2 个义项：可被微生物降解）；句意：这种包装可完全降解，因此可以和厨余一起埋掉。

pos.zh: 可分解的；可降解的；可拆解的

senses.title: Able to be split chemically
senses.definition: describing a compound that can be separated into simpler substances
senses.definitionCN: 描述可被分离成更简单物质的化合物
senses.example: The solvent is decomposable at high temperature into two gases.
senses.exampleCN: 这种溶剂在高温下可分解为两种气体。
senses.why: The suffix -able adds possibility to the verb, so the adjective says the breakdown can happen rather than that it has happened.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -able 给动词加上「可能」，因此形容词说的是分解「可以发生」，而不是已经发生。

senses.title: Able to be biodegraded
senses.definition: describing material that microbes can break down within a reasonable time
senses.definitionCN: 描述微生物能在合理时间内分解的材料
senses.example: The bag is decomposable in a home compost bin.
senses.exampleCN: 这种袋子在家庭堆肥桶中可降解。
senses.why: Environmental writing uses the adjective for materials designed to disappear through microbial action.
senses.whyCN: 环保写作使用这个形容词来描述被设计成可通过微生物作用消失的材料。

senses.title: Able to rot away
senses.definition: describing dead organic matter that will decay naturally
senses.definitionCN: 描述会自然腐烂的死亡有机物
senses.example: All the garden waste here is decomposable within a year.
senses.exampleCN: 这里所有的花园废弃物都能在一年内腐烂。
senses.why: The adjective generalizes the chemistry of decay to any organic material, without naming the microbes.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词把腐烂的化学过程泛化到任何有机材料，而不点名微生物。

senses.title: Able to be taken apart
senses.definition: describing a structure or device whose parts can be separated
senses.definitionCN: 描述其部件可被分离的结构或装置
senses.example: The shelter is decomposable into panels one person can carry.
senses.exampleCN: 这座棚屋可拆解成一个人能搬运的板材。
senses.why: Mechanical use extends the same possibility from molecules to parts, where separation is physical rather than chemical.
senses.whyCN: 机械义项把同样的「可能性」从分子扩展到部件，分离成了物理过程而非化学过程。

senses.title: Able to be factored
senses.definition: describing a mathematical object that can be expressed as a product or sum of simpler objects
senses.definitionCN: 描述可表示成更简单对象之乘积或和的数学对象
senses.example: The matrix is decomposable into two triangular factors.
senses.exampleCN: 这个矩阵可分解为两个三角因子。
senses.why: Mathematics borrows the adjective for objects whose structure permits a standard split.
senses.whyCN: 数学借用这个形容词描述结构上允许标准拆分的对象。

senses.title: Able to be modularised
senses.definition: in computing, describing a system that can be divided into independent modules
senses.definitionCN: 计算机领域描述可划分为独立模块的系统
senses.example: The old monolith is not easily decomposable into services.
senses.exampleCN: 这个旧单体系统不容易拆分成若干服务。
senses.why: Software architecture treats decomposability as a design property, so the adjective judges systems rather than substances.
senses.whyCN: 软件架构把「可分解性」当作设计属性，因此这个形容词评判的是系统而不是物质。

senses.title: Suitable for composting
senses.definition: describing waste that a composting system can accept and process
senses.definitionCN: 描述堆肥系统可以接收并处理的废弃物
senses.example: Only decomposable cutlery is allowed at the festival.
senses.exampleCN: 节日上只允许使用可堆肥处理的餐具。
senses.why: Waste management narrows the general property to what a particular facility can actually process.
senses.whyCN: 废弃物管理把这一泛化属性收窄为「某套设施实际能处理」的范围。

senses.title: Able to be analysed apart
senses.definition: figuratively, describing a complex idea or institution that can be separated into understandable parts
senses.definitionCN: 比喻描述可拆成可理解部分的复杂观念或机构
senses.example: The problem is decomposable into three decisions, not one big one.
senses.exampleCN: 这个问题可以拆成三个决定，而不是一个大决定。
senses.why: The analytic sense treats understanding as a form of breakdown, keeping the parts-and-whole structure.
senses.whyCN: 分析义把理解视为一种分解，仍保留「部分与整体」的结构。

intro.en: Decomposable is decompose plus the Latin-derived English ending -able.
intro.cn: decomposable 是 decompose 加上源自拉丁语的英语词尾 -able。

items.en: The suffix -able continues Latin -abilis, 'capable of being', built on the verb stem plus -bilis. It entered English through French -able.
items.cn: 后缀 -able 承自拉丁语 -abilis「能够被……的」，由动词词干加 -bilis 构成，经法语 -able 进入英语。

items.en: Decompose itself came from French décomposer, built on de- and componere 'to put together'.
items.cn: decompose 本身来自法语 décomposer，建立在 de- 与 componere「放在一起」之上。

items.en: Nineteenth-century chemistry needed adjectives for substances that could be separated, and decomposable joined a large family of -able technical terms.
items.cn: 19 世纪的化学需要形容词来描述可被分离的物质，decomposable 加入了庞大的 -able 技术术语家族。

items.en: Late twentieth-century packaging and waste debates made decomposable a common label for biodegradable products. The exact first use in advertising is not documented here.
items.cn: 20 世纪后期的包装与废弃物争论使 decomposable 成为可降解产品的常见标签。广告中的确切首用此处不作断言。

items.en: Mathematics and software engineering later applied the adjective to objects and systems whose structure allows a clean split.
items.cn: 数学与软件工程随后把这个形容词用于结构上允许干净拆分的对象与系统。

note.en: The first group is the same family in other forms; the second holds related material labels.
note.cn: 第一组是同一词族的其他形式；第二组是相关的材料标签。

entries.definition: The action; decomposable describes the capacity, not the act.
entries.definitionCN: 指动作；decomposable 描述能力，而不是动作。

entries.definition: The process itself; decomposable says the process can occur.
entries.definitionCN: 指过程本身；decomposable 说明该过程可以发生。

entries.definition: The organism or device that does it; the adjective never names an agent.
entries.definitionCN: 执行分解的生物或装置；形容词不指施动者。

entries.definition: Breakable down by living organisms; decomposable is broader because it can also mean chemical or mechanical separation.
entries.definitionCN: 可被生物分解的；decomposable 范围更宽，还可指化学或机械分离。

entries.definition: Able to break down in a composting system to usable soil; stricter than decomposable.
entries.definitionCN: 可在堆肥系统中分解为可用土壤；比 decomposable 要求更严。

entries.definition: Designed to be thrown away after use; it says nothing about whether the item will break down.
entries.definitionCN: 设计为用后即弃；并不说明该物品是否会分解。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: -able as possibility and the material labels.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：-able 表示可能性，以及相关的材料标签。

normal.en: -able = can be: decompose + able = can be decomposed.
normal.cn: -able 表示「可以被」：decompose + able = 可以被分解。

normal.en: The word joins a family: biodegradable, compostable, recyclable.
normal.cn: 这个词属于一个家族：biodegradable、compostable、recyclable。

normal.en: The ordinary phrase is fully decomposable, common on packaging.
normal.cn: 常见搭配是 fully decomposable，常见于包装标识。

normal.en: The noun decomposability names the property itself.
normal.cn: 名词 decomposability 指这种性质本身。

normal.en: The same adjective works for a compound, a bag, a panel, a matrix or a plan.
normal.cn: 同一个形容词可用于化合物、袋子、板材、矩阵或计划。

abstract.en: Think of a sugar cube in tea: the question is not whether it is sweet but whether it can disappear.
abstract.cn: 想象茶里的方糖：问题不是它甜不甜，而是它能不能消失。

abstract.en: A decomposable plan is one that can be reduced to steps small enough to start.
abstract.cn: 可拆解的计划，就是能缩小到足以立刻开始的若干步骤的计划。

abstract.en: Packaging that says decomposable is making a promise about time, not about material.
abstract.cn: 标注可分解的包装，承诺的是时间，而不是材料。

examples.en: The new trays are decomposable in commercial compost.
examples.cn: 这种新托盘在商业堆肥中可分解。

examples.en: Not every plastic labelled decomposable breaks down in seawater.
examples.cn: 并非所有标为可分解的塑料都能在海水中降解。

examples.en: The model is decomposable into two independent modules.
examples.cn: 这个模型可拆分为两个独立模块。

dict_mnemonic.text: decompose（分解）+ able（能……的）→ 能分解的 → 可降解的

root: decompose（拉丁语 de-「分开」+ componere「放在一起」；经法语进入英语）+ 拉丁语 -abilis「能够被……的」（英语 -able）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all state a capacity: a compound, a material, dead matter, a structure, a matrix, a system, waste and an idea can each be taken apart.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在陈述一种能力：化合物、材料、死亡物质、结构、矩阵、系统、废弃物与观念都可以被拆开。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a whole that is able to come apart when the right force is applied.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个在施加合适力量时能够散开的整体。

branches.en: THE CORE: possibility is attached to a compound or to dead matter that will decay.
branches.cn: 核心：可能性附着在化合物或终将腐烂的死亡物质上。

branches.en: THE MATERIAL LABEL: microbiology and waste management ask what a facility can actually process.
branches.cn: 材料标签：微生物学与废弃物管理关心的是设施实际能处理什么。

branches.en: THE OBJECT: a built thing can be separated into parts by hand.
branches.cn: 实物：人造物可以被手工拆成部件。

branches.en: THE STRUCTURE: matrices and software systems are judged by whether they admit a clean split.
branches.cn: 结构：矩阵与软件系统按「是否允许干净拆分」来评判。

branches.en: THE IDEA: a complex problem is decomposable into decisions small enough to take.
branches.cn: 观念：复杂问题可以拆成小到足以做出的决定。

intro.en: Decomposable is a verb base plus a suffix of possibility.
intro.cn: decomposable 是动词词基加表示可能性的后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies de- 'apart', ponere 'place' and -abilis 'able to be'; the -able ending reached English through French.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了 de-「分开」、ponere「放置」与 -abilis「能够被……」，其中 -able 经法语进入英语。

items.example: The film is decomposable in soil.
items.exampleCN: 这种薄膜在土壤中可分解。

items.example: Decomposition takes longer in dry soil.
items.exampleCN: 干燥土壤中的分解更慢。

items.example: A decomposer consumes the dead leaves.

items.exampleCN: biodegradable 比 decomposable 范围更窄。

items.example: The label says compostable, not merely decomposable.
items.exampleCN: 标签写的是「可堆肥」，而不仅是「可分解」。

items.meaning: able to be processed and reused
items.example: Recyclable and decomposable are different claims.
items.exampleCN: 「可回收」与「可分解」是两种不同的宣称。

items.meaning: able to last, the opposite capacity
items.meaningCN: 能持久的，是相反的能力
items.example: Durable goods resist the breakdown that decomposable ones allow.
items.exampleCN: 耐用品抵抗分解，而可分解物品允许分解。

definition_zh: 饿极了的；贪婪的；贪得无厌的
definition_en: extremely hungry, or eager to consume something in large amounts
core_image: 一个人盯着桌上的面包，眼睛比手先动
scene: 队伍两天没吃东西，一见到面包就扑了上去。 After two days without food, the group fell on the bread like ravenous animals.
sceneCN: 这里 ravenous 指饿极了的（第 1 个义项：极度饥饿）；句意为队伍两天没吃东西，一见到面包就扑了上去。

pos.zh: 饿极了的；贪婪的；贪得无厌的

senses.title: Extremely hungry
senses.definition: so hungry that food fills the mind and the body moves before it thinks
senses.definitionCN: 饿到食物占满头脑、身体先于思考而动
senses.example: After two days without food, the group fell on the bread like ravenous animals.
senses.exampleCN: 两天没吃东西之后，队伍像饿极了的野兽一样扑向面包。
senses.why: This is the physical sense, and it keeps the violence of the Latin root inside a hungry body.
senses.whyCN: 这是身体的一层，它把拉丁词根里的那股猛劲留在饥饿的身体上。

senses.title: Greedily eager for something
senses.titleCN: 贪婪渴求的；贪得无厌的
senses.definition: eager to take in something other than food, such as news, power or resources, in amounts that cannot be satisfied
senses.definitionCN: 对食物以外的东西（消息、权力、资源）渴求到无法满足
senses.example: The reporters were ravenous for any detail of the case.
senses.exampleCN: 记者们贪求这个案子的一切细节。
senses.why: The hunger moves from stomach to another appetite, while the word keeps its taking edge.
senses.whyCN: 饥饿从胃移到了另一种欲望上，而那个伸手就拿的锋芒还在。

intro.en: Ravenous comes from Latin ravinosus, 'given to seizing', from ravere, a form linked to rapacity.
intro.cn: ravenous 来自拉丁语 ravinosus（惯于夺取的），与表示掠夺的词相关。

items.en: Rapere meant to seize and carry off.
items.cn: rapere 意为抓住带走。

items.en: Ravina named a rushing or a seizure.
items.cn: ravina 指猛冲或夺取。

items.en: The adjective described a seizing hunger.
items.cn: 这个形容词描述夺取般的饥饿。

items.en: English used ravenous for extreme hunger.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪用 ravenous 指极度饥饿。

items.en: The word now also describes greedy use of resources.
items.cn: 今天这个词也描述对资源的贪婪使用。

note.en: The look-alike group is the raven- family; the near-meaning group separates starving, famished, voracious and insatiable.
note.cn: 形近组是 raven 词族；近义组把「濒饿的」「饿坏的」「贪婪的」「无法满足的」分开。

entries.definition: a large black bird.
entries.definitionCN: 一种黑色大鸟。

entries.definition: talking wildly.
entries.definitionCN: 胡言乱语的。

entries.definition: a deep narrow valley.
entries.definitionCN: 深窄的山谷。

entries.definition: with extreme hunger.
entries.definitionCN: 饿极地。

entries.definition: suffering from lack of food.
entries.definitionCN: 因缺食而受苦的。

entries.definition: very hungry indeed.
entries.definitionCN: 非常饥饿的。

entries.definition: eating or wanting great amounts.
entries.definitionCN: 食量或欲望极大的。

entries.definition: impossible to satisfy.
entries.definitionCN: 无法满足的。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a hand reaching before the mind has spoken.
normalIntro.cn: 以下联想留住「手在头脑开口之前先伸出去」的画面。

normal.en: Ravenous shares a root with ravenous beasts and rapacity: hunger that grabs.
normal.cn: ravenous 与掠夺同根：会抓取的饥饿。

normal.en: Picture a loaf on a table and a whole group moving at once.
normal.cn: 想象桌上一条面包，一整群人在同一刻动起来。

normal.en: Say RAV-e-nus; the middle sounds like ravine.
normal.cn: 读 RAV-e-nus，中间听起来像 ravine。

normal.en: The word can describe appetite for food, news or water use.
normal.cn: 这个词可以描述对食物、消息或水资源的胃口。

normal.en: Ask whether the hunger is a body or a system.
normal.cn: 问一句：这饥饿属于一具身体，还是一个系统？

abstract.en: Ravenous describes need that has begun to look like appetite.
abstract.cn: ravenous 描述一种已经开始像胃口的需要。

abstract.en: The word makes hunger active: it reaches, it takes, it does not wait.
abstract.cn: 这个词让饥饿变成主动的：它伸手、它拿取、它不等。

abstract.en: Every economy has a ravenous edge where demand outruns supply.
abstract.cn: 每个经济体都有一条贪婪的边，那里需求跑在供给前面。

examples.en: The long walk gave the children a ravenous appetite.
examples.cn: 长途步行让孩子们胃口大开。

examples.en: The reporters were ravenous for any detail of the case.
examples.cn: 记者们急于吞下这个案子的任何细节。

examples.en: The city's ravenous consumption of water emptied the reservoir.
examples.cn: 这座城市对水的贪婪消耗掏空了水库。

dict_mnemonic.text: raven（猛夺）+ ous（充满）→ 饿得像要抢食一样。

root: 拉丁语 rapere（夺取）→ ravinosus（惯于夺取的）

sensesIntro.en: Ravenous has two senses: a body made violent by hunger, and a hunger of the mind that no amount can satisfy.
sensesIntro.cn: ravenous 有两层：被饥饿变得凶猛的身体，以及任何数量都无法满足的头脑之饥。

core.en: A HAND REACHING FIRST
core.cn: 先伸出去的手

branches.en: The body that reaches before it thinks.
branches.cn: 先伸手、后思考的身体。

branches.en: Bread, and hands moving at once.
branches.cn: 面包，以及同时伸出的手。

branches.en: Hunger moved to news, books or resources.
branches.cn: 饥饿移向消息、书本或资源。

branches.en: Food in one sense, everything else in the other.
branches.cn: 一层是食物，另一层是食物之外的一切。

branches.en: A hunger that consumption cannot end.
branches.cn: 消耗无法终止的饥饿。

intro.en: The ravenous family is built on grabbing: ravenous, ravenously and ravenousness all keep the sense of a hunger that takes.
intro.cn: ravenous 词族建立在抓取上：ravenous、ravenously、ravenousness 都保留「会拿取的饥饿」这层意思。

latinIntro.en: Latin rapere, 'to seize', gives ravina and ravinosus; the English word kept the violence and lost the Latin noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 rapere（夺取）给出 ravina 与 ravinosus；英语保留暴力感，丢掉了拉丁名词。

definition_zh: 地理学家；研究地理的人
definition_en: a person who studies geography, especially its spatial patterns, environments, or maps
core_image: 一位背着测量仪的人沿河谷行走，边看地形边记录
scene: 一位研究者背着测量仪沿河谷行走，每到一处就记录河道宽度与坡度： A geographer walked the valley, recording the width and slope of the river.
sceneCN: 这里 geographer 指「研究地理的人；地理学家」（第 1 个义项：以地理学为业的人）；句意为一位地理学家沿河谷行走，记录河宽与坡度。

pos.zh: 地理学家；地理研究者（可数，复数为 geographers）

senses.title: A person who studies geography
senses.definition: a scholar or professional whose field is the study of places, environments, and spatial patterns
senses.definitionCN: 以地方、环境与空间格局为研究领域的学者或专业人员
senses.example: A geographer walked the valley, recording the width and slope of the river.
senses.exampleCN: 一位地理学家沿河谷行走，记录河宽与坡度。
senses.why: The -er ending marks the practitioner, so geographer is simply 'one who does geography'.
senses.whyCN: -er 结尾标记从业者，因此 geographer 就是「做地理学的人」。

senses.title: A physical geographer
senses.definition: a geographer who studies landforms, climate, water, soils, or ecosystems
senses.definitionCN: 研究地貌、气候、水、土壤或生态系统的地理学家
senses.example: The physical geographer measured how the glacier had retreated.
senses.exampleCN: 这位自然地理学家测量了冰川退缩的距离。
senses.why: The field divides, and each specialist carries the parent job title with an adjective.
senses.whyCN: 学科分支化后，每位专家都在母职称前加一个形容词。

senses.title: A historical mapmaker
senses.definition: an early geographer whose work was chiefly describing coasts and drawing maps
senses.definitionCN: 工作主要是描述海岸与绘制地图的早期地理工作者
senses.example: The geographer drew a coast that later explorers corrected.
senses.exampleCN: 这位地理学家画出的海岸线后来被探险者修正。
senses.why: Before geography became a university science, its practitioners were often mapmakers and compilers.
senses.whyCN: 在地理学成为大学科学之前，其实践者往往是制图者与编纂者。

senses.title: A human geographer
senses.definition: a geographer who studies cities, economies, cultures, or migration
senses.definitionCN: 研究城市、经济、文化或迁移的地理学家
senses.example: The human geographer interviewed families who had moved inland.
senses.exampleCN: 这位人文地理学家访谈了迁往内陆的家庭。
senses.why: People also make spatial patterns, so the same job title covers the study of settlements and movement.
senses.whyCN: 人同样制造空间格局，因此同一职称也涵盖聚落与迁移研究。

senses.title: A regional describer
senses.definition: someone who systematically describes the lands, peoples, and resources of a region
senses.definitionCN: 系统描述某一地区土地、人群与资源的人
senses.example: The geographer wrote a full account of the province's rivers.
senses.exampleCN: 这位地理学家写下了该省河流的完整记述。
senses.why: The oldest sense is descriptive: to write down what is there, region by region.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的含义是描述性的：一个地区一个地区地写下那里有什么。

senses.title: A geography teacher
senses.definition: a teacher who instructs students in geography
senses.definitionCN: 向学生教授地理学的教师
senses.example: The geographer at the school ran the map club.
senses.exampleCN: 学校里的地理老师负责地图社团。
senses.why: A discipline's name plus -er can also name the person who teaches it, especially in school usage.
senses.whyCN: 学科名加 -er 也可指教授它的人，尤其在学校语境中。

senses.title: A GIS or remote-sensing specialist
senses.titleCN: 地理信息系统或遥感专业人员
senses.definition: a geographer whose work uses satellite data, digital maps, and spatial analysis
senses.definitionCN: 使用卫星数据、数字地图与空间分析工作的地理学家
senses.example: The geographer turned satellite images into a flood-risk map.
senses.exampleCN: 这位地理学家把卫星影像转成洪水风险图。
senses.why: New instruments change the job while the old title stays, so geographer now includes digital mapping.
senses.whyCN: 新工具改变工作内容，旧职称却保留，因此地理学家如今也包括数字制图。

senses.title: Figurative: a person who knows a place
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：熟悉某地格局的人
senses.definition: someone who understands the layout and social map of a place very well
senses.definitionCN: 非常了解某地布局与社会地图的人
senses.example: As a geographer of the city, she knew every shortcut and every border.
senses.exampleCN: 作为熟悉这座城市的人，她知道每条捷径与每条边界。
senses.why: The metaphor promotes anyone with deep spatial knowledge to the rank of a geographer.
senses.whyCN: 这一比喻把任何具备深厚空间知识的人提升到「地理学家」的位置。

intro.en: Geographer comes from Greek through Latin, meaning 'one who writes about the earth'. The elements are clear; the deeper origin of ge is not. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: geographer 经拉丁语来自希腊语，意为「书写大地的人」。语素清楚，但 ge 的更深来源不明。年代均为约数。

items.en: Geographos meant 'one who describes the earth', built on ge 'earth' and graphein 'to write'.
items.cn: geographos 意为「描述大地的人」，由 ge「大地」与 graphein「书写」构成。

items.en: The element ge is of uncertain origin and is often regarded as pre-Greek; any Indo-European root offered for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 语素 ge 来源不确定，常被视为前希腊语词；为它提出的任何印欧词根都属重构形式。

items.en: Latin borrowed geographus for a writer on geography, and English took the word through French in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入 geographus 指地理著述者，英语在 16 世纪经法语借入。

items.en: As geography became a university subject, geographer shifted from a writer of descriptions to a trained researcher.
items.cn: 随着地理学成为大学学科，geographer 从描述写作者转为受过训练的研究者。

items.en: Satellite and digital mapping added new roles in the twentieth century; the first use of geographer for these specialists is not precisely dated.
items.cn: 卫星与数字制图在 20 世纪增添了新角色，地理学家用于指这些专家的最早年代没有精确记载。

note.en: Group one holds job and subject words from the same Greek stock; group two holds specialists in neighbouring fields.
note.cn: 第一组是同出希腊语词干的职业与学科词；第二组是相邻领域的专家。

entries.definition: The field itself; geographer is the person who practises it.
entries.definitionCN: 学科本身；geographer 是从事它的人。

entries.definition: Relating to geography; it modifies nouns but does not name a person.
entries.definitionCN: 与地理学有关；它修饰名词，但不指人。

entries.definition: The fuller adjective variant; it never replaces the noun for a person.
entries.definitionCN: 较长的形容词变体；它不能替代指人的名词。

entries.definition: The study of rocks and earth structure; its practitioner is a geologist, not a geographer.
entries.definitionCN: 研究岩石与地球结构的学科；其从业者是 geologist，而非 geographer。

entries.definition: A person who designs and draws maps; many geographers map, but cartography is a distinct skill.
entries.definitionCN: 设计并绘制地图的人；许多地理学家会制图，但制图是一门独立技能。

entries.definition: A person who studies rocks, minerals, and the earth's interior rather than surface places.
entries.definitionCN: 研究岩石、矿物与地球内部而非地表地方的人。

entries.definition: A person who measures land boundaries and elevations; the work supplies data that geographers use.
entries.definitionCN: 测量土地边界与高程的人；其工作为地理学家提供数据。

entries.definition: A person who travels into unknown regions; early explorers often supplied geography with its descriptions.
entries.definitionCN: 进入未知地区旅行的人；早期探险者常为地理学提供描述材料。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Greek morphemes, real professions and real collocations, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实希腊语素、真实职业与真实搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Geography is the field; geographer is the person; geographic is the adjective.
normal.cn: geography 是学科，geographer 是人，geographic 是形容词。

normal.en: The -er ending marks the practitioner, as in teacher and mapper.
normal.cn: -er 结尾标记从业者，如 teacher 与 mapper。

normal.en: A geographer may be physical, human, economic, or digital.
normal.cn: 地理学家可以是自然的、人文的、经济的或数字的。

normal.en: Early geographers were often mapmakers and regional describers.
normal.cn: 早期地理学家往往是制图者与区域描述者。

normal.en: The Greek source geographos literally means earth-writer.
normal.cn: 希腊语来源 geographos 字面就是「书写大地的人」。

abstract.en: Picture a person who carries a map in the head instead of the hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人把地图装在心里，而不是拿在手上。

abstract.en: Picture someone who can feel a border before seeing it.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人还没看见边界，就能感觉到它。

abstract.en: Picture a guide whose directions are really a description of the land.
abstract.cn: 想象一位向导，他的指路其实是对大地的描述。

examples.en: A geographer walked the valley, recording the width and slope of the river.
examples.cn: 一位地理学家沿河谷行走，记录河宽与坡度。

examples.en: The geographer compared rainfall records from a hundred stations.
examples.cn: 这位地理学家比较了一百个站点的降水记录。

examples.en: A human geographer studied how the new road changed village life.
examples.cn: 一位人文地理学家研究了新公路如何改变村庄生活。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「geo（大地）+ grapher（书写者）」——书写大地的人 → 地理学家

root: 拉丁语 geographus，来自希腊语 geographos = ge「大地」+ graphein「书写」+ -os（人）。ge 更深来源不确定；graphein 词根清楚。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the general practitioner to physical and human specialists, historical mapmakers, regional describers, teachers, digital specialists, and finally to anyone who knows a place deeply.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一般从业者走到自然与人文专家、历史制图者、区域描述者、教师、数字专家，最后落到任何深谙某地的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person walking a valley with instruments, writing down what the land does.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人带着仪器走在河谷里，记录大地的表现。

branches.en: RESEARCHER AND TEACHER: the same title covers those who advance the field and those who teach it.
branches.cn: 研究者与教师：同一职称既指推进学科的人，也指教授它的人。

branches.en: TWO BRANCHES: physical and human geographers split the living surface between them.
branches.cn: 两个分支：自然与人文地理学家把活的地表一分为二。

branches.en: DESCRIPTION AND MAP: the oldest tasks were writing down regions and drawing their coasts.
branches.cn: 描述与地图：最古老的任务是记述区域与描画海岸。

branches.en: NEW INSTRUMENTS: satellites and digital maps extend the craft without renaming it.
branches.cn: 新工具：卫星与数字地图扩展了技艺，却未改变职称。

branches.en: METAPHOR: deep knowledge of a place is treated as a professional qualification.
branches.cn: 比喻：对某地的深刻了解被当作一种专业资格。

intro.en: Geographer is a Greek compound plus the English agent suffix -er, so its structure is easy to read.
intro.cn: geographer 是希腊语复合词加英语施事后缀 -er，结构容易读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin geographus is the borrowed intermediate; Greek ge and graphein are the ultimate elements.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 geographus 是借入的中间形式；希腊语 ge 与 graphein 是最终语素。

items.example: Geography is what the geographer practises.
items.exampleCN: 地理学是地理学家从事的学问。

items.example: The geographer mapped the old river channels.
items.exampleCN: 这位地理学家标绘了古河道。
这位地理学家使用了地理数据。

items.example: The two sites are geographically close.
items.exampleCN: 两处地点在地理上很近。

items.meaningCN: 研究岩石的学科；地质学
items.example: A geologist, not a geographer, studies deep rock.
items.exampleCN: 研究深部岩石的是地质学家，而非地理学家。

items.example: Cartographers turn survey data into maps.
items.exampleCN: 制图者把测量数据变成地图。

latinEntries.structure: geographus, geographi (m., second declension), from Greek

definition_zh: 出口商；出口国；报关出口方；导出程序或导出工具
definition_en: a person, firm or country that sells or sends goods out to another country
core_image: 码头尽头一位商人把提单递给船长，身后是已经装好的本国货物，船将驶向海外
scene: 出口码头上，一位商人把提单递给船长，身后的本国货物已经全部装船。 The exporter handed over the bill of lading before the ship left for overseas buyers.
sceneCN: 这里指「把货物卖到境外的出口商」，对应第 1 个义项：向另一国买方售出并运出货物的一方；句意为这位出口商在船离港前把提单交给船长。画面要点：码头、提单、已装船的本国货物、远处的船身。

pos.zh: 出口商；出口方（可数，指公司、个人或国家）

derivatives.zh: 出口（exporter 的基础动词，去掉施动后缀即得，指把货物搬出去）
出口行为（export 加表示动作的名词后缀，指过程而非人）
可出口的（export 加表示可能的形容词后缀，指允许或能够外销）
多个出口方（exporter 加复数后缀，语义由单方转为多方）
报关出口方（exporter 加 of record 构成的法定称谓，指登记在案的出口责任方）

senses.title: A firm that sells goods abroad
senses.titleCN: 把货物卖到境外的公司
senses.definition: a business that sells and ships its goods to buyers in other countries
senses.definitionCN: 把货物卖给另一国买方并运出的企业
senses.example: The exporter handed over the bill of lading before the ship left for overseas buyers.
senses.exampleCN: 这位出口商在船离港前把提单交给船长。
senses.why: Export is the act of carrying goods out, and the agent suffix names the party performing it, so exporter is 'the one who sends out'.
senses.whyCN: export 是把货物搬出去的动作，施动后缀指执行者，因此 exporter 就是「把货送出去的那一个」。

senses.title: A country that sells more than it buys
senses.titleCN: 出口大于进口的国家或地区
senses.definition: a country or region whose sales abroad exceed its purchases from abroad
senses.definitionCN: 向外售出多于从境外购入的国家或地区
senses.example: The country is a net exporter of copper and a net importer of wheat.
senses.exampleCN: 该国是铜的净出口方、小麦的净进口方。
senses.why: Trade balances are counted at the level of economies, so a whole country can be called a party that exports.
senses.whyCN: 贸易差额在经济体层面计算，于是整个国家也能被称作出口的一方。

senses.title: The party legally responsible at customs
senses.titleCN: 在海关承担法律责任的报关出口方
senses.definition: the party registered as legally responsible for goods leaving the country
senses.definitionCN: 在货物出境时被登记为承担法律责任的一方
senses.example: The exporter of record filed the declaration before loading.
senses.exampleCN: 报关出口方在装船前提交了申报。
senses.why: Each shipment needs one accountable name, so the commercial role hardened into a customs status.
senses.whyCN: 每票货物都需要一个可追责的名字，商业角色于是固化为海关身份。

senses.title: A seller of power or fuel to another grid
senses.titleCN: 向其他电网或市场售电、售燃料的一方
senses.definition: a utility, region or country that sells electricity or fuel beyond its own system
senses.definitionCN: 向本系统之外售出电力或燃料的公用事业、地区或国家
senses.example: The province became a net exporter of electricity after the dams were built.
senses.exampleCN: 水坝建成后，该省成为电力净出口方。
senses.why: Energy flows across grid boundaries like cargo across borders, and the sending side takes the same label.
senses.whyCN: 能源像货物过境一样跨过电网边界，送出的一端得到同样的称呼。

senses.title: A tool that writes data out
senses.titleCN: 把数据写出去的导出程序
senses.definition: a routine or feature that saves data from an application in an outside format
senses.definitionCN: 把应用中的数据保存成外部格式的程序或功能
senses.example: The exporter writes the results to a plain text file.
senses.exampleCN: 导出程序把结果写进一个纯文本文件。
senses.why: Software names the routine as if it were a party, so the tool that sends data out is an exporter.
senses.whyCN: 软件把这个程序当作一方来命名，于是把数据送出去的工具就叫 exporter。

senses.title: A body that spreads cultural practices
senses.titleCN: 向外传播文化做法的人或机构
senses.definition: a person or institution that carries its own practices or ideas to other places
senses.definitionCN: 把自身做法或观念带到别处的个人或机构
senses.example: The conservatory became an exporter of a distinctive teaching style.
senses.exampleCN: 这所音乐学院成了一种独特教学风格的传播者。
senses.why: The outward motion survives without money: influence, too, can be shipped.
senses.whyCN: 向外动作不需要金钱也能成立：影响力同样可以被「运出去」。

senses.title: A producer of one commodity for foreign sale
senses.titleCN: 为外销生产某一商品的生产方
senses.definition: a farm, mine or producer that supplies a single commodity to foreign markets
senses.definitionCN: 向外国市场供应单一商品的农场、矿山或生产者
senses.example: The region is the world's largest exporter of lentils.
senses.exampleCN: 该地区是世界上最大的扁豆出口方。
senses.why: Commodity chains need a named origin, so the producer at the head of the chain is called the exporter.
senses.whyCN: 商品链需要一个具名的源头，于是链条最前端的生产者被称为出口方。

senses.title: The selling side of a trade contract
senses.titleCN: 贸易合同中的卖方一方
senses.definition: the party in a sales contract that sells and delivers the goods
senses.definitionCN: 买卖合同中出售并交付货物的一方
senses.example: The exporter covers insurance under the agreed terms.
senses.exampleCN: 按约定条款，出口方负责投保。
senses.why: Contracts prefer role names, so exporter serves as shorthand for the seller who ships.
senses.whyCN: 合同偏好角色名称，因此 exporter 成为「负责发运的卖方」的简称。

intro.en: Exporter is export plus the English agent suffix -er, so it names the doer of an outward carrying. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: exporter 是 export 加英语施动后缀 -er 构成，为「向外搬运」这一动作的执行者命名。年代均为约数。

items.en: Exportare 'to carry out' supplied the verb, built on ex- 'out' and portare 'to carry'.
items.cn: exportare「搬出去」提供动词，由 ex-「向外」与 portare「搬运」构成。

items.en: The suffix -er descends from Old English -ere and is the native means of naming a doer.
items.cn: 后缀 -er 源自古英语 -ere，是英语本族为执行者命名的手段。

items.en: As export settled into trade, exporter named the merchant who sold and shipped to foreign buyers.
items.cn: 随着 export 在贸易中固定下来，exporter 指向外国买方销售并发运的商人。

items.en: Customs law created the party of record, while trade statistics applied the word to whole economies.
items.cn: 海关法确立登记方，贸易统计则把这个词用到整个经济体上。

items.en: Software later borrowed the word for routines that write data out of an application.
items.cn: 软件随后借用这个词，指把数据写出应用程序的程序。

note.en: The first group shares the outward carrying stem or looks close to it; the second group names parties that also sell or ship.
note.cn: 第一组共享「向外搬运」词干或与之外形相近；第二组是同样销售或发运的一方。

entries.definition: The act of sending goods out; only the suffix turns it into a party.
entries.definitionCN: 把货物送出的动作；只有加上后缀才成为一方。

entries.definition: The procedure of exporting; it names the flow, while exporter names who causes it.
entries.definitionCN: 出口的程序；它指流动，而 exporter 指促成流动的人。

entries.definition: The same suffix on the opposite prefix: the party that buys and receives from abroad.
entries.definitionCN: 同一后缀加相反前缀：从境外买入并接收货物的一方。

entries.definition: A harbour, from Latin portus, not from portare; an exporter may use a port, but the words are unrelated.
entries.definitionCN: 港口，出自拉丁 portus，并非 portare；出口商可能用港口，但两个词并无同源关系。

entries.definition: Anyone who sells; exporter adds that the buyer is abroad and the goods must leave the country.
entries.definitionCN: 任何卖方；exporter 额外说明买方在境外、货物必须离境。

entries.definition: A firm that provides goods to buyers; it may sell at home, while an exporter sells across a border.
entries.definitionCN: 向买方提供货物的公司；它可以在国内销售，而出口商跨越国界销售。

entries.definition: The party that arranges or performs the carriage; an exporter may also be the shipper, but the roles are distinct.
entries.definitionCN: 安排或执行运输的一方；出口商可能同时是发货人，但两个角色不同。

entries.definition: The selling party in a transaction or contract; exporter is the trade-specific narrowing of that role.
entries.definitionCN: 交易或合同中的卖方；exporter 是这一角色在贸易中的具体化。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real verb, the real suffix and real trade roles.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的动词、真实的后缀与真实贸易角色。

normal.en: Export plus -er: the party that carries goods out.
normal.cn: export 加 -er：把货物搬出去的那一方。

normal.en: The suffix marks a doer, so exporter can sign, invoice and be audited.
normal.cn: 后缀标出执行者，因此出口商能签字、开票、被审计。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the roles: net exporter, major exporter, exporter of record.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出角色：净出口方、主要出口商、报关出口方。

normal.en: The counterpart is importer, the same suffix on the opposite prefix.
normal.cn: 对应词是 importer，同一后缀加在相反的前缀上。

normal.en: An exporter sells outward; the goods, not the money, does the travelling.
normal.cn: 出口商向外销售；出行的是货物，不是钱。

abstract.en: Picture one signature at the end of a pier that sends a whole shipment on its way.
abstract.cn: 想象码头尽头一个签名，就把整票货物送上了路。

abstract.en: Picture a country drawn as a seller standing at the border with a full cart.
abstract.cn: 想象一个国家被画成站在边境、推着满车货物的卖方。

abstract.en: Picture a program packing its records into a box and pushing it out the door.
abstract.cn: 想象一个程序把记录装进箱子，推出门外。

examples.en: The exporter shipped the order two weeks ahead of schedule.
examples.cn: 出口商比计划提前两周发出了订单。

examples.en: Brazil is a major exporter of soybeans.
examples.cn: 巴西是大豆的主要出口国。

examples.en: The exporter of record must retain the shipping documents.
examples.cn: 报关出口方必须保存运输单据。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「往外搬的人」——export 是搬出去，加个表示人的尾巴，就是负责卖到境外的那一方 → 出口商

root: export「出口」+ -er（英语本族施动后缀，源自古英语 -ere），指执行出口的人、公司或国家；同根动词出自拉丁 exportare。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all name a party: a trading firm, a national economy, a customs debtor, an energy seller, a software routine, a cultural carrier, a commodity producer and the selling side of a contract.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项指的都是某一方：贸易公司、国家经济、海关义务人、能源卖方、软件程序、文化传播者、商品生产者，以及合同中的卖方。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one merchant at a pier handing a bill of lading to a captain.
core.cn: 核心意象：码头边一位商人把提单递给船长。

branches.en: BASE DOER: the suffix turns carrying out into a business role.
branches.cn: 基础施动者：后缀把「搬出去」变成商业角色。

branches.en: WHOLE ECONOMIES: a country or grid acts as one seller.
branches.cn: 整体经济：国家或电网被当作单一卖方。

branches.en: LEGAL PARTY: customs and contracts need one named seller to carry liability.
branches.cn: 法律一方：海关与合同都需要一个具名卖方来承担责任。

branches.en: SYSTEM OUTPUT: software names its writing routine as a doer.
branches.cn: 系统出口：软件把写数据的程序也称作施动者。

branches.en: BEYOND GOODS: ideas and single commodities are sent out by the same kind of party.
branches.cn: 货物之外：观念与单一商品也由同类一方送出。

intro.en: Exporter combines a Latin verb of outward carrying with the native English suffix for doers.
intro.cn: exporter 把拉丁语表示向外搬运的动词，与英语本族的施动后缀组合起来。

latinIntro.en: Latin portare 'to carry' supplies the stem and gives export, import, transport and portable; the agent suffix is English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 portare「搬运」提供词干，并衍生 export、import、transport 与 portable；施动后缀则来自英语。

items.example: They export wool to two markets.
items.exampleCN: 他们把羊毛出口到两个市场。

items.example: The suffix turns actions into parties.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动作变成一方。
出口商们抗议这项新税。

items.meaning: allowed or able to be exported
items.example: The fruit is exportable after inspection.

items.exampleCN: 进口商办理了货物进境手续。

definition_zh: n. 恶化；变坏；退化；（材料的）劣化
definition_en: the process of becoming progressively worse in condition, quality or value
core_image: 墙上的裂缝一年比一年宽；体检报告上的箭头连续三次朝上
scene: 病情出现了恶化。 There was a deterioration in his condition.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：deterioration 指恶化；句意是病情出现了恶化。

pos.zh: 恶化；变坏；退化

senses.title: A process of getting worse
senses.definition: the process of becoming progressively worse
senses.definitionCN: 逐渐变得更糟的过程
senses.example: There was a deterioration in his condition.
senses.exampleCN: 病情出现了恶化。
senses.why: A wall crack wider than it was last year.
senses.whyCN: 一道比去年更宽的墙缝。

senses.title: A fall in quality or value
senses.definition: a decline in the quality, value or strength of something
senses.definitionCN: 某物的质量、价值或强度下降
senses.example: The report noted a deterioration in service.
senses.exampleCN: 报告指出服务质量下降。
senses.why: An arrow pointing down on a results chart.
senses.whyCN: 成绩图表上一个向下的箭头。

senses.title: Damage to a material
senses.definition: the physical breaking down of a material over time
senses.definitionCN: 材料随时间发生的物理性损坏
senses.example: Deterioration of the pipes caused the leak.
senses.exampleCN: 管道劣化导致了漏水。
senses.why: A rusty pipe flaking at a joint.
senses.whyCN: 接口处正在剥落锈片的管道。

intro.en: Deterioration comes from Latin deteriorare, to make worse, from deterior, worse, built with de- down and the comparative ending -ter.
intro.cn: deterioration 源自拉丁语 deteriorare（使变坏），来自 deterior（更坏的），由 de-（向下）加比较级后缀 -ter 构成。

items.en: De meant down or away.
items.cn: de 意为向下、离开。

items.en: Deterior meant worse, lower than before.
items.cn: deterior 意为更坏的、比从前低的。

items.en: Deteriorare meant to make worse.
items.cn: deteriorare 意为使变坏。

items.en: Deteriorate entered English first as a verb.
items.cn: 十六世纪 deteriorate 先以动词进入英语。

items.en: Deterioration followed as the noun of the process.
items.cn: 十八世纪 deterioration 作为过程名词随之出现。

items.en: It is now standard in medical and technical reports.
items.cn: 如今它是医疗与技术报告中的标准用词。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the deterior- worse family and the -terior ending; the near-meaning group names other words for getting worse.
note.cn: 形近组共享 deterior-（更坏）家族与 -terior 结尾；近义组是其他表示「变糟」的词。

entries.definition: To become worse; it is the verb behind this noun.
entries.definitionCN: 变坏；是这个名词背后的动词。

entries.definition: The inside of something; it shares the -terior ending but not the worse sense.
entries.definitionCN: 某物的内部；共享 -terior 结尾，但没有「更坏」的意思。

entries.definition: The outside of something; it shares -terior but concerns position, not quality.
entries.definitionCN: 某物的外部；共享 -terior，但关乎位置而非质量。

entries.definition: A gradual loss of quality, strength or value.
entries.definitionCN: 质量、力量或价值的逐渐下降。

entries.definition: The process of rotting or breaking down.
entries.definitionCN: 腐烂或分解的过程。

entries.definition: The process of becoming worse in quality or condition.
entries.definitionCN: 质量或状况变差的过程。

normalIntro.en: Deterioration is deterior- worse plus -ation process: the process of moving further down.
normalIntro.cn: deterioration 就是 deterior-（更坏）加 -ation（过程）：一步步往下走的过程。

normal.en: Deterior means worse in Latin.
normal.cn: deterior 在拉丁语里意为更坏。

normal.en: -ation turns the verb into a process noun.
normal.cn: -ation 把动词变成过程名词。

normal.en: Deterioration in health is a set phrase.
normal.cn: deterioration in health 是固定搭配。

normal.en: It is usually uncountable.
normal.cn: 它通常不可数。

normal.en: Interior shares the ending, not the meaning.
normal.cn: interior 共享结尾，但不共享意思。

abstract.en: A wall crack wider than it was last year.
abstract.cn: 一道比去年更宽的墙缝。

abstract.en: An arrow pointing down on a results chart.
abstract.cn: 成绩图表上一个向下的箭头。

abstract.en: A rusty pipe flaking at a joint.
abstract.cn: 接口处正在剥落锈片的管道。

examples.en: Doctors watched for any deterioration.
examples.cn: 医生留意任何恶化迹象。

examples.en: The deterioration of the bridge was slow.
examples.cn: 这座桥的劣化是缓慢的。

examples.en: We must prevent further deterioration.
examples.cn: 我们必须防止进一步恶化。

dict_mnemonic.text: deterioration ＝ deterior（更坏的，拉丁语 de「向下」＋比较级 -ter）＋ -ation（过程名词）＝一步步往下变坏的过程，「恶化」。

root: 拉丁语 de（向下）＋比较级后缀 -ter → deterior（更坏的）→ deteriorare（使变坏）→ deterioratio → 英语 deterioration

sensesIntro.en: One thing going down: a wall crack, a service chart and a rusty pipe.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一件往下走的东西：一道墙缝、一张服务图表与一根锈管。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wall crack wider than it was last year, with the arrow on the report still pointing down
core.cn: 核心意象：一道比去年更宽的墙缝，报告上的箭头仍朝下

branches.en: A wall crack wider than it was last year.
branches.cn: 一道比去年更宽的墙缝。

branches.en: An arrow pointing down on a results chart.
branches.cn: 成绩图表上一个向下的箭头。

branches.en: A rusty pipe flaking at a joint.
branches.cn: 接口处正在剥落锈片的管道。

branches.en: Both show a steady move downward.
branches.cn: 两者都显示持续向下的走势。

branches.en: Both name a loss of usable quality.
branches.cn: 两者都指可用质量的丧失。

intro.en: Deterioration is deterior- plus -ation; the worse stem also builds deteriorate.
intro.cn: deterioration 由 deterior- 加 -ation 构成；更坏这个词干也造出 deteriorate。

latinIntro.en: Latin deterior means worse, interior inner and exterior outer.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 deterior 意为更坏的，interior 意为内部的，exterior 意为外部的。

definition_zh: 色谱法；色谱分析
definition_en: a laboratory method that separates the components of a mixture by passing it through a medium in which the components move at different rates
core_image: 一滴墨点在滤纸条下端，水慢慢爬上去，墨散成几道不同颜色的带
scene: 课堂上，学生把一滴墨点在滤纸条下端，水沿纸面慢慢上升，墨迹散成几道颜色不同的带。 Chromatography separated the ink into its component dyes.
sceneCN: 这里 chromatography 指利用各组分移动速度不同而分离混合物的方法（第 1 个义项：色谱法）；句意为色谱法把墨水分离成几种染料成分。图中可辨识物件：滤纸条、墨点、水槽、颜色分层。

pos.zh: 色谱法；色谱分析（不可数）
色谱分离操作（可数，少见）

senses.title: Separation by different rates of movement
senses.titleCN: 按不同移动速度分离混合物的方法
senses.definition: a method in which a mixture is carried through a stationary medium so that its components separate because they travel at different speeds
senses.definitionCN: 让混合物通过固定介质，各组分因移动速度不同而分开的方法
senses.example: Chromatography separates the pigments in a leaf extract.
senses.exampleCN: 色谱法把叶片提取液中的色素分开。
senses.why: the word joins Greek khrōma 'colour' to graphein 'to write', because the first separations wrote coloured bands onto paper.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把希腊 khrōma「颜色」与 graphein「写」连起来，因为最早的分离把彩色色带「写」在纸上。

senses.title: A paper or thin-layer method
senses.definition: a simple form of the method in which a solvent climbs a paper or a coated plate and leaves separated spots behind
senses.definitionCN: 一种简单形式：溶剂沿纸或涂层板爬升，留下分开的斑点
senses.example: Paper chromatography showed two distinct spots.
senses.exampleCN: 纸色谱显示出两个清晰的斑点。
senses.why: the general method is named after its simplest visible form, where a coloured spot literally climbs a sheet of paper.
senses.whyCN: 这个总称来自它最简单、可见的形式：一个有色斑点真的沿纸面往上爬。

senses.title: Gas chromatography
senses.definition: a form of the method in which a vaporized sample is carried by a gas through a column
senses.definitionCN: 把汽化样品用气体载过色谱柱的一种形式
senses.example: Gas chromatography identified the volatile compounds.
senses.exampleCN: 气相色谱鉴定出了挥发性化合物。
senses.why: the carrier can be a gas as easily as a liquid, and the name stays the same because the separating principle is unchanged.
senses.whyCN: 载流可以是气体也可以是液体，名称不变，因为分离原理没变。

senses.title: Liquid chromatography
senses.definition: a form of the method in which a liquid carries the sample through a packed column
senses.definitionCN: 用液体把样品载过填充柱的一种形式
senses.example: Liquid chromatography is standard for drug analysis.
senses.exampleCN: 液相色谱是药物分析的标准方法。
senses.why: liquids were the first carriers, and the modern high-pressure version keeps the old name.
senses.whyCN: 液体是最早的载流，现代高压版本也沿用旧名。

senses.title: One run and its recorded trace
senses.titleCN: 一次色谱分离及其记录曲线
senses.definition: a single separation run and the pattern of peaks or spots that records where each component ended up
senses.definitionCN: 一次分离运行，以及记录各组分最终位置的峰形或斑点
senses.example: The chromatography produced three peaks.
senses.exampleCN: 这次色谱分离产生了三个峰。
senses.why: a method that can be run repeatedly becomes a countable operation, and the trace makes the result visible.
senses.whyCN: 可反复运行的方法成为可数操作，而记录曲线让结果可见。

senses.title: An identification technique
senses.titleCN: 用于鉴定与定量的分析技术
senses.definition: the technique used to identify a substance or measure how much of it is present by comparing its position or peak
senses.definitionCN: 通过比较位置或峰来鉴定物质、测量其含量的技术
senses.example: Forensic labs rely on chromatography to identify traces.
senses.exampleCN: 法医实验室依靠色谱法鉴定微量痕迹。
senses.why: separation alone only divides; comparison against known standards turns the division into identification.
senses.whyCN: 分离本身只是分开；与已知标准比较，才把分开变成鉴定。

senses.title: A classroom separation of colours
senses.titleCN: 课堂上分离色素的实验
senses.definition: the school experiment in which ink or leaf pigment is separated into visible coloured bands
senses.definitionCN: 把墨水或叶片色素分成可见色带的课堂实验
senses.example: The students used chromatography to separate ink colours.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们用色谱法分离墨水的颜色。
senses.why: the original demonstration was also a lesson, so the word keeps a place in teaching long after the instruments grew complex.
senses.whyCN: 最初的演示本身也是一堂课，因此仪器变复杂很久之后，这个词仍在教学里占一席。

senses.title: Sorting a mixed whole by affinity
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：按亲和差异把混杂整体分开
senses.definition: used figuratively of any process that lets the parts of a mixed whole reveal themselves at different speeds or affinities
senses.definitionCN: 比喻指让混杂整体的各部分按不同速度或亲和力自行显现的过程
senses.example: The committee's chromatography of proposals separated the serious from the decorative.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会对提案的「色谱分离」，把认真的与装饰性的分开了。
senses.why: the abstract sense keeps the geometry of a column: what sticks travels slowly, what does not sticks goes ahead.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义保留色谱柱的几何：附着得牢的走得慢，不附着的先走。

intro.en: Chromatography was coined in 1906 by the Russian botanist Mikhail Tsvet from Greek khrōma 'colour' and graphein 'to write', for his method of separating plant pigments on paper. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: chromatography 由俄国植物学家米哈伊尔·茨维特于一九〇六年用希腊 khrōma「颜色」与 graphein「写」造出，指他在纸上分离植物色素的方法。年代均为约数。

items.en: Khrōma meant 'colour, skin, surface', with the stem khrōmat-; it also names the colour of a thing as opposed to its substance.
items.cn: khrōma 意为「颜色、皮肤、表面」，词干为 khrōmat-；它指事物的颜色，与其实体相对。

items.en: Graphein meant 'to write, draw, record', and its combining form -graphia names a way of writing or recording.
items.cn: graphein 意为「写、画、记录」，其组合形式 -graphia 命名一种书写或记录方式。

items.en: Tsvet combined the two elements to name a method that wrote coloured bands onto paper while separating leaf pigments.
items.cn: 茨维特把这两个成分组合起来，命名一种在纸上「写出」彩色色带、从而分离叶片色素的方法。

items.en: English adopted the term in the early twentieth century, at first for the paper method and then for any separation by differing rates.
items.cn: 英语在二十世纪初采用这个术语，先指纸上方法，后指任何按不同速度进行的分离。

items.en: From the mid-twentieth century gas and liquid versions turned the word into a family of techniques with columns, detectors and recorded peaks.
items.cn: 二十世纪中叶起，气相与液相版本把这个词变成一族技术，配有色谱柱、检测器与记录峰。

items.en: Source uncertain (first publication): accounts differ between 1903 and 1906 for the first published description, so the earlier date is not treated as fixed.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首次发表）：关于最早发表描述的时间，有资料记作一九〇三年，也有记作一九〇六年，因此较早的年份不作为定论。

note.en: Group one holds the instrument, the trace and the words built on the same Greek elements; group two holds other separation techniques used beside it.
note.cn: 第一组是仪器、记录图以及用同一希腊成分构成的词；第二组是常与它并用的其他分离技术。

entries.definition: The instrument that performs the separation; chromatography is the method.
entries.definitionCN: 执行分离的仪器；chromatography 是方法。

entries.definition: The printed trace of peaks produced by a run; it is the result, not the method.
entries.definitionCN: 一次运行产生的峰形记录；是结果，不是方法。

entries.definition: The metal named for its brightly coloured compounds; it shares khrōma but has nothing to do with separation.
entries.definitionCN: 因化合物色彩鲜艳而得名的金属；共享 khrōma，但与分离无关。

entries.definition: Khrōma plus sōma 'body': the stained bodies seen in a cell nucleus, named for how they take dye.
entries.definitionCN: khrōma 加 sōma「体」：细胞核中被染色的体，因摄取染料而得名。

entries.definition: Separation of charged molecules in an electric field; it is used beside chromatography for proteins and DNA.
entries.definitionCN: 在电场中分离带电分子；常与色谱法并用于蛋白质与脱氧核糖核酸的分析。

entries.definition: Identification of substances by the light they absorb or emit; it can confirm what chromatography separated.
entries.definitionCN: 通过吸收或发射的光鉴定物质；可确认色谱法分出的东西。

entries.definition: Separation by spinning, which pulls heavier parts outward; it sorts by density rather than affinity.
entries.definitionCN: 通过旋转分离，把较重的部分甩向外侧；按密度而非亲和力分选。

entries.definition: Separation by a barrier that holds back particles; it removes solids but does not divide dissolved components.
entries.definitionCN: 用屏障截留颗粒的分离；能去除固体，但不分开已溶解的组分。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Khrōma 'colour' plus graphein 'write': colour written onto paper.
normal.cn: khrōma「颜色」加 graphein「写」：把颜色写在纸上。

normal.en: The family runs chromatography, chromatograph, chromatogram, chromatographic.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 chromatography、chromatograph、chromatogram、chromatographic。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the forms: gas chromatography, liquid chromatography, paper chromatography.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出形式：气相色谱、液相色谱、纸色谱。

normal.en: The colour root also appears in chromium and chromosome, which share the name but not the method.
normal.cn: 颜色词根也出现在 chromium 与 chromosome 中，共享名称而不共享方法。

normal.en: The method depends on one rule: what sticks travels slowly, what does not sticks races ahead.
normal.cn: 这个方法只依赖一条规则：附着得牢的走得慢，不附着的跑在前。

abstract.en: Picture a drop of ink climbing paper and breaking into bands of colour.
abstract.cn: 想象一滴墨沿纸面爬升，裂成几道色带。

abstract.en: Picture runners on a track, some held back by mud and some free.
abstract.cn: 想象跑道上的选手，有些被泥拖住，有些不受阻。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd leaving a hall, the fastest out first and the slowest still talking.
abstract.cn: 想象人群离开大厅，最快的先出去，最慢的还在说话。

examples.en: Chromatography is used to test athletes for banned substances.
examples.cn: 色谱法被用来检测运动员体内的违禁物质。

examples.en: The lab ran the sample through gas chromatography and compared the peaks.
examples.cn: 实验室让样品通过气相色谱，并比较峰形。

examples.en: Students separated the colours of a marker pen by chromatography.
examples.cn: 学生们用色谱法分离了记号笔的颜色。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「chroma（颜色）+ graphy（写）」——把颜色写成一条条色带：色谱法

root: 希腊 khrōma（颜色，词干 khrōmat-）+ graphein（写）+ -ia（方法名词）；一九〇六年由茨维特为纸上分离植物色素的方法造出，早期发表年份有存疑。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one separation: components travel at different rates, a paper version makes that visible, gas and liquid carriers do the same, a run leaves a trace, the trace identifies a substance, a classroom shows it with ink, and finally any mixed whole can be sorted by affinity.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着同一次分离：各组分以不同速度前行，纸上版本让它可见，气体与液体载流做同样的事，一次运行留下记录，记录能鉴定物质，课堂上用墨水演示，最后任何混杂整体都能按亲和力分选。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a drop of ink on paper breaking into coloured bands as the solvent climbs.
core.cn: 核心意象：纸上的一滴墨，随溶剂爬升裂成几道彩色带。

branches.en: THE PRINCIPLE AND ITS SIMPLEST DEMO: different speeds separate the mixture, and paper makes that visible.
branches.cn: 原理与最简单的演示：不同速度分开混合物，纸让它看得见。

branches.en: CARRIERS: gas and liquid are two ways of moving the sample, not two different principles.
branches.cn: 载流：气体与液体是两种运送样品的方式，不是两套原理。

branches.en: THE RECORD: one run and its trace turn a separation into evidence.
branches.cn: 记录：一次运行及其曲线，把分离变成证据。

branches.en: IDENTIFICATION AND TEACHING: comparison names the substance, and the school version keeps the method visible.
branches.cn: 鉴定与教学：比较给出名称，课堂版本让方法保持可见。

branches.en: SORTING A WHOLE: what sticks to the medium travels slowly, which is a way to read any mixed body.
branches.cn: 分选整体：附着于介质的走得慢，这可以用来解读任何混杂体。

intro.en: Chromatography is a modern compound of two Greek elements, and each element also builds many scientific words.
intro.cn: chromatography 是由两个希腊成分构成的现代复合词，每个成分也构成许多科学词。

latinIntro.en: Greek khrōma 'colour' gives chromium, chromosome and chromatid; graphein 'to write' gives -graphy, graph, diagram and photograph.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 khrōma「颜色」构成 chromium、chromosome 与 chromatid；graphein「写」构成 -graphy、graph、diagram 与 photograph。

senses.why: The noun keeps the sense of a sworn league.

senses.title: To join in a league

definition_zh: 烈火；火焰；光辉； blazing 般的爆发；v. 燃烧；发光；开拓
definition_en: a strong bright fire, or to burn brightly and fiercely
core_image: 正午烈日下腾起的一团火光
scene: 干柴堆被点燃，火光冲天而起。 The fire blazed through the dry forest all night.
sceneCN: 这里 blaze 是「熊熊燃烧」（第 2 个义项：猛烈而明亮地燃烧）；句意是大火在干燥的森林里烧了整夜。

pos.zh: 烈火；光辉；爆发
燃烧；发光；开创

senses.title: A bright, strong fire
senses.definition: a large, brightly burning fire
senses.definitionCN: 大而明亮燃烧的火
senses.example: Firefighters fought the blaze for hours.
senses.exampleCN: 消防员与大火搏斗了几个小时。
senses.why: The Germanic root means to blow or shine; strong fire is the concrete core.
senses.whyCN: 日耳曼词根本指吹气或发亮，烈火是其具体核心。

senses.title: To burn brightly
senses.definition: to burn fiercely and with bright light
senses.definitionCN: 猛烈燃烧、放出强光
senses.example: The fire blazed through the dry forest all night.
senses.exampleCN: 大火在干燥的森林里烧了整夜。
senses.why: The noun made into a verb keeps the sense of fierce, visible burning.
senses.whyCN: 名词转动词，保留猛烈而可见的燃烧之义。

senses.title: A burst of bright light or colour
senses.definition: a brilliant display of light or colour
senses.definitionCN: 光或色的炫目爆发
senses.example: The garden was a blaze of colour in May.
senses.exampleCN: 五月的花园满园绚烂。
senses.why: Bright fire and bright colour are read by the same eye.
senses.whyCN: 明亮的火与明亮的色，在眼中是同一种「亮」。

senses.title: To shine intensely
senses.definition: to give out strong light, as eyes or the sun
senses.definitionCN: 发出强光，如眼睛或太阳
senses.example: Anger blazed in her eyes.
senses.exampleCN: 怒火在她眼中燃烧。
senses.why: Eyes that flash feel as hot as fire to the observer.
senses.whyCN: 闪光的眼睛在观者眼中如火焰般灼热。

senses.title: A sudden outburst of emotion
senses.definition: a sudden powerful showing of feeling or violence
senses.definitionCN: 情感或暴力的骤然强烈表露
senses.example: The speech set off a blaze of outrage.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇讲话激起了轩然大波的愤怒。
senses.why: Emotion burns like fire; the metaphor is the oldest fire we know.
senses.whyCN: 情感如火燃烧，这是人类最古老的火之隐喻。

senses.title: A mark cut on a tree to mark a path
senses.definition: a mark made on a tree to show a trail
senses.definitionCN: 刻在树上用于标示路径的痕迹
senses.example: Hikers followed the white blazes along the trail.
senses.exampleCN: 远足者沿着路上的白色路标前行。
senses.why: A blaze of the axe strips bark in a flash of pale wood.
senses.whyCN: 斧头一击剥落树皮，露出一片亮白的木色，故称 blaze。

senses.title: To pioneer a new path
senses.definition: to be the first to explore or develop something new
senses.definitionCN: 率先探索或开辟新领域
senses.example: She blazed a trail for women in engineering.
senses.exampleCN: 她为女性进入工程界开辟了道路。
senses.why: Pioneers cut trail marks; to blaze a trail is to chop the first path.
senses.whyCN: 先驱者砍刻路标，blaze a trail 即砍出第一道路径。

senses.title: To shoot continuously
senses.definition: to fire guns rapidly and continuously
senses.definitionCN: 用枪连续快速射击
senses.example: The soldiers blazed away at the targets.
senses.exampleCN: 士兵们朝目标连续射击。
senses.why: Muzzle flashes are little blazes, and firing repeats them.
senses.whyCN: 枪口火光如小火焰，连发便是火焰连绵。

definition_zh: 邪恶的；违法的；穷凶极恶的
definition_en: extremely wicked, especially in a way that breaks moral or legal limits
core_image: 一份写在暗处的名单，每个名字后面都标着日期和价钱
scene: 那份合同看上去合法，条款里却藏着一条专门用来骗老人的安排。 The nefarious scheme was hidden in plain language.
sceneCN: 这里 nefarious 指邪恶的（第 2 个义项：卑劣的计谋）；句意为这个恶计藏在平实的措辞里。

pos.zh: 邪恶的；违法的；穷凶极恶的

senses.title: Wicked beyond the law
senses.definition: evil of a kind that violates what is held sacred or lawful
senses.definitionCN: 违反被视为神圣或合法之界限的那种恶
senses.example: The nefarious scheme was hidden in plain language.
senses.exampleCN: 这个恶计藏在平实的措辞里。
senses.why: The word is stronger than merely illegal: it adds a violation of what should never be done.
senses.whyCN: 这个词比「仅仅违法」更强：它加上了一层对「本不该做之事」的违犯。

senses.title: A nefarious scheme
senses.definition: a plan built to harm others while appearing harmless
senses.definitionCN: 为伤害他人而建、却显得无害的计划
senses.example: The nefarious scheme was hidden in plain language.
senses.exampleCN: 这个恶计藏在平实的措辞里。
senses.why: A plan becomes nefarious when its success depends on someone not understanding it.
senses.whyCN: 当一个计划的成功依赖他人看不懂它时，这个计划就是卑劣的。

senses.title: A nefarious trade
senses.definition: an activity or business that profits from what should not be sold
senses.definitionCN: 从本不该被出售之物中获利的行为或生意
senses.example: The nefarious trade in stolen documents continued for years.
senses.exampleCN: 被盗文件的黑市交易持续了多年。
senses.why: Commerce can be orderly and still nefarious, because the harm sits in the goods, not the paperwork.
senses.whyCN: 生意可以井然有序而仍然邪恶，因为伤害在货里，不在文书里。

senses.title: Nefarious intent
senses.definition: a purpose that aims at another person's harm
senses.definitionCN: 以伤害他人为目标的用意
senses.example: The message looked friendly but carried a nefarious intent.
senses.exampleCN: 这条消息看似友好，却带着恶意。
senses.why: Intent is invisible, so the word is often applied to what a message was meant to do rather than what it said.
senses.whyCN: 意图不可见，因此这个词常用来指一条消息想要做的事，而不是它说出口的话。

senses.title: A nefarious alliance
senses.definition: a partnership formed for a purpose no honest party would join
senses.definitionCN: 为任何正当一方都不愿加入的目的而形成的伙伴关系
senses.example: The two firms formed a nefarious alliance to fix prices.
senses.exampleCN: 两家公司组成邪恶联盟来操纵价格。
senses.why: The word judges the purpose, not the members, which is why it can describe respectable people.
senses.whyCN: 这个词评判的是目的，而非成员，因此它也能形容体面的人。

senses.title: Nefarious means
senses.definition: methods that are condemned even when the goal is arguable
senses.definitionCN: 即使目标尚可争论也仍受谴责的方法
senses.example: They used nefarious means to reach a defensible end.
senses.exampleCN: 他们用卑劣手段去达到一个尚可辩护的目的。
senses.why: Separating ends from means is an old habit, and the word refuses to do it quietly.
senses.whyCN: 把目的与手段分开是旧习惯，而这个词拒绝安静地配合。

senses.title: A nefarious reputation
senses.definition: the public name a person or group earns by such acts
senses.definitionCN: 一个人或团体因这类行为得到的公众名声
senses.example: The family carried a nefarious reputation into the next generation.
senses.exampleCN: 这家人把恶名带进了下一代。
senses.why: A reputation is the shadow a past act casts forward, and the word keeps that shadow attached to a name.
senses.whyCN: 名声是过去行为向前投下的影子，这个词让这道影子继续挂在一个名字上。

senses.title: The banality of the nefarious
senses.definition: the fact that great harm is often done by ordinary, orderly people
senses.definitionCN: 巨大的伤害常由普通而有秩序的人完成这一事实
senses.example: The nefarious part was not dramatic; it was a form signed without reading.
senses.exampleCN: 邪恶之处并不戏剧化；它是一份没读就签的表。
senses.why: The word can be most useful when it points at routine, not at monsters.
senses.whyCN: 当它指向日常流程而不是怪物时，这个词可能最有用。

intro.en: Nefarious comes from Latin for contrary to divine law, and it once meant simply impious.
intro.cn: nefarious 来自拉丁语「违反神法」，最初只指不敬神。

items.en: Nefarius meant wicked, abominable, outside what is permitted.
items.cn: nefarius 意为「邪恶的、可憎的、超出许可的」。

items.en: Nefas meant an unspeakable wrong, a thing against divine law.
items.cn: nefas 意为「不可言说的罪」，违反神法之事。

items.en: Fas meant divine law or right, so nefas was its negation.
items.cn: fas 意为神法、正当，因此 nefas 是它的否定。

items.en: English took the adjective in the 16c. and kept the sense of exceeding all limits.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入这个形容词，保留了「逾越一切界限」的意思。

items.en: Modern English softened it toward wicked or criminal, often with a slight dramatic air.
items.cn: 现代英语把它软化为「邪恶或犯罪」，常带一点戏剧气。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin wrong root; the near-meaning group ranks kinds of evil.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语「不正」的词根；近义组排列恶的种类。

entries.definition: in a wicked manner.
entries.definitionCN: 以邪恶的方式。

entries.definition: extreme wickedness.
entries.definitionCN: 穷凶极恶。

entries.definition: a thing contrary to divine law.
entries.definitionCN: 违反神法之事。

entries.definition: too wicked to be spoken of.
entries.definitionCN: 邪恶到不可言说。

entries.definition: bad in a way that harms deliberately.
entries.definitionCN: 故意害人的恶。

entries.definition: suggesting evil or harm to come.
entries.definitionCN: 暗示邪恶或即将来临的伤害。

entries.definition: extremely unjust or morally wrong.
entries.definitionCN: 极不公正或道德败坏的。

entries.definition: behaving like a storybook villain.
entries.definitionCN: 像故事里的恶人。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a list kept in the dark, with dates and prices beside each name.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想留住「一份藏在暗处的名单，每个名字旁都有日期和价钱」的画面。

normal.en: Nefarious contains nefas, Latin for a thing against divine law.
normal.cn: nefarious 含 nefas，拉丁语「违反神法之事」。

normal.en: Think of a contract that is legal in form and rotten in purpose.
normal.cn: 想象一份形式合法、目的腐烂的合同。

normal.en: Say nuh-FAIR-ee-us; the middle sounds like a polite word for an ugly thing.
normal.cn: 读成 nuh-FAIR-ee-us，中间音像用客气话包装丑事。

normal.en: Link with infamous: both name a reputation, one earned by evil.
normal.cn: 和 infamous 联系：两者都指名声，一个由恶行挣得。

normal.en: Pair it with scheme: nefarious rarely describes a person alone.
normal.cn: 和 scheme 配对：nefarious 很少单独形容一个人。

abstract.en: The strongest evil often wears the clothes of ordinary procedure.
abstract.cn: 最强的恶，常穿着日常程序的衣服。

abstract.en: A word like this warns us to look at purpose, not at manners.
abstract.cn: 这样的词提醒我们看目的，而不是看礼貌。

abstract.en: What is legal and what is permitted are not the same question.
abstract.cn: 合法与「被允许」不是同一个问题。

examples.en: The nefarious scheme was hidden in plain language.
examples.cn: 这个恶计藏在平实的措辞里。

examples.en: The nefarious trade in stolen documents continued for years.
examples.cn: 被盗文件的黑市交易持续了多年。

examples.en: They used nefarious means to reach a defensible end.
examples.cn: 他们用卑劣手段去达到一个尚可辩护的目的。

dict_mnemonic.text: ne（不）+ far（神法、正当）+ ious：不合神法，就是「邪恶的」。

root: 拉丁语 nefas（违反神法之事），加形容词后缀 -ius

sensesIntro.en: Nefarious judges purpose rather than paperwork; the senses differ in whether the evil sits in a plan, a trade, an intention or a reputation.
sensesIntro.cn: nefarious 评判的是目的而非文书；各义项的差别在于恶在计谋、交易、用意，还是名声里。

core.en: EVIL THAT HIDES IN ORDER
core.cn: 藏在秩序里的恶

branches.en: Schemes and methods judged by what they do.
branches.cn: 按所为来评判的计谋与手段。

branches.en: Trades that profit from what should not be sold.
branches.cn: 从不该被出售之物获利的交易。

branches.en: Intention and partnership formed for harm.
branches.cn: 为伤害而形成的用意与伙伴关系。

branches.en: The reputation left behind.
branches.cn: 留下的名声。

branches.en: The ordinary, signed, unread form of harm.
branches.cn: 伤害那种普通、已签字、未被阅读的形态。

intro.en: The nefas family is a pair of opposites: fas is what is right, and nefas is what may not be done.
intro.cn: nefas 词族是一对反面：fas 是正当，nefas 是不许做的事。

latinIntro.en: Latin fas names divine law; the negative ne- turns it into a prohibition that no human court invented.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fas 命名神法；否定成分 ne- 把它变成一条并非人间法庭发明的禁令。

items.exampleCN: 这一行为的邪恶令他们震惊。

Fas allowed the rite to continue.

items.exampleCN: 记录了一桩不可言说的罪。
