items.exampleCN: 那座恶名昭彰的建筑被拆了。

definition_zh: 热力学；研究热、功与能量相互转换的物理学分支
definition_en: the branch of physics that studies heat, work and the conversion between them
core_image: 一只蒸汽机的汽缸里，热气推着活塞向前滑动，热量被换算成推动机器的功
scene: 物理实验室里，老师指着蒸汽机模型讲解活塞的运动，说 Thermodynamics explains why the piston moves when steam expands.
sceneCN: 这里 thermodynamics 指「研究热与功相互转换的物理学分支」（第 1 个义项：把热、功与能量放进同一套规律）；句意为热力学解释了蒸汽膨胀时活塞为何移动。图中可辨识物件：蒸汽机模型、活塞、压力表、温度计。

pos.zh: 热力学（学科名，不可数，作主语时谓语用单数）
某套热力学分析或能量账目（引申用法）

derivatives.zh: 热力学的；与热和功的转换有关的
热力学的（较少用的形容词变体）
从热力学角度看；在热力学意义上

senses.title: The science of heat and work
senses.titleCN: 研究热与功相互转换的物理学分支
senses.definition: the branch of physics that deals with heat, work and the conversion between them
senses.definitionCN: 研究热、功以及二者相互转换的物理学分支
senses.example: The steam engine gave nineteenth-century physicists their first practical problem in thermodynamics.
senses.exampleCN: 蒸汽机给十九世纪的物理学家提供了第一个热力学实际问题。
senses.why: Greek thermē 'heat' plus dynamis 'power' names the field that turns heat into usable work.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 thermē「热」加 dynamis「力」，命名的正是把热变成可用功的学问。

senses.title: Energy is conserved in every process
senses.definition: the principle that energy can change form but can neither be created nor destroyed in an isolated system
senses.definitionCN: 在一个孤立系统中，能量可以改变形式，但既不能凭空产生也不能凭空消失
senses.example: The first law of thermodynamics rules out any machine that produces work from nothing.
senses.exampleCN: 热力学第一定律排除了任何凭空产生功的机器。
senses.why: The law is an accounting rule: heat added, work done and internal energy must balance to zero.
senses.whyCN: 这条定律是一本账：加入的热、对外做的功与内能变化必须收支相抵。

senses.title: Processes run in one direction
senses.titleCN: 第二定律：熵增与过程的不可逆
senses.definition: the principle that entropy in an isolated system never decreases, so spontaneous processes have a preferred direction
senses.definitionCN: 孤立系统的熵永不减少，因此自发过程具有固定的进行方向
senses.example: The second law of thermodynamics explains why heat never flows by itself from a cold cup to a hot one.
senses.exampleCN: 热力学第二定律解释了热量为何不会自己从冷杯子流向热杯子。
senses.why: Once energy is spread out, gathering it back would require extra work, and the law states that this cannot happen on its own.
senses.whyCN: 能量一旦散开，重新聚拢就需要额外做功，而这条定律正是说它不会自行发生。

senses.title: Analysis of engines and efficiency
senses.definition: the applied study of cycles that convert heat into mechanical work and of the limits on their efficiency
senses.definitionCN: 研究把热转换为机械功的循环过程及其效率上限的应用学问
senses.example: Engineers use thermodynamics to decide how much of a turbine's heat can become electricity.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师用热力学来判断涡轮机里的热量能有多少变成电能。
senses.why: The field grew from the practical need to measure how much work a boiler and piston could deliver.
senses.whyCN: 这门学问起源于实际需要：测量锅炉与活塞究竟能输出多少功。

senses.title: Heat changes in chemical reactions
senses.titleCN: 化学热力学：反应热与反应方向
senses.definition: the branch that predicts the heat released or absorbed by chemical reactions and the direction they can take
senses.definitionCN: 预测化学反应放出或吸收的热量，以及反应可进行方向的分支
senses.example: Chemical thermodynamics tells chemists whether a reaction will warm the flask or chill it.
senses.exampleCN: 化学热力学告诉化学家一个反应会让烧瓶变热还是变冷。
senses.why: When reactions replaced steam as the main source of questions, the same energy accounting was applied to bonds.
senses.whyCN: 当化学反应取代蒸汽成为主要问题来源，同一套能量账目被套用到化学键上。

senses.title: From molecules to bulk properties
senses.titleCN: 统计热力学：从微观粒子推出宏观性质
senses.definition: the branch that derives temperature, pressure and entropy from the statistical behaviour of very many particles
senses.definitionCN: 由大量粒子的统计行为推出温度、压强与熵的分支
senses.example: Statistical thermodynamics links the average speed of molecules to the pressure on a container wall.
senses.exampleCN: 统计热力学把分子的平均速率与容器壁受到的压强联系起来。
senses.why: Temperature is not a property of one molecule but of a crowd, so the laws are rebuilt from counting arrangements.
senses.whyCN: 温度不是单个分子的属性，而是一群分子的属性，因此定律要从排列组合的计数重建。

senses.title: A ledger of gains and losses
senses.titleCN: 比喻义：把任何系统当作能量或精力的账本
senses.definition: a way of describing any system as a balance of energy or effort coming in and going out
senses.definitionCN: 把任何系统描述为能量或精力进出相抵的一种说法
senses.example: The coach treated the team's season as a lesson in thermodynamics, counting every ounce of fatigue.
senses.exampleCN: 教练把球队的赛季当成一堂热力学课，把每一分疲劳都记在账上。
senses.why: The figurative use keeps the accounting core: nothing enters or leaves the ledger unnoticed.
senses.whyCN: 比喻用法保留了记账这一核心：没有任何投入或损耗能不被记下。

senses.title: A course or textbook subject
senses.titleCN: 作为课程或教材的学科名
senses.definition: the academic subject taught under this name, usually alongside mechanics and chemistry
senses.definitionCN: 以此命名的学校课程，通常与力学、化学并列开设
senses.example: Thermodynamics is a required course for students of mechanical engineering.
senses.exampleCN: 热力学是机械工程专业学生的必修课。
senses.why: As a discipline name ending in -ics, it is treated as singular and takes a singular verb.
senses.whyCN: 作为以 -ics 结尾的学科名，它被当作单数，谓语动词也用单数。

intro.en: Thermodynamics is a nineteenth-century scientific compound built from two Greek nouns, thermē 'heat' and dynamis 'power', plus the subject suffix -ics. It has no inherited Latin ancestor; the Latin-looking ending is only the international scientific convention.
intro.cn: thermodynamics 是 19 世纪的科学复合词，由两个希腊名词 thermē「热」与 dynamis「力」加学科后缀 -ics 构成。它没有拉丁语祖传形式，看似拉丁的词尾只是国际科学命名惯例。

items.en: Thermē meant 'heat' and is related to thermos 'warm, hot'. Its origin before Greek is not established, so any older Indo-European form offered for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: thermē 意为「热」，与 thermos「温暖的、热的」相关。它在希腊语之前的来源未得到证明，凡为其提出的更早印欧形式均属重构形式。

items.en: Dynamis meant 'power, force, capacity', from dynasthai 'to be able'. The same root gives English dynamic and dynamite.
items.cn: dynamis 意为「力量、能力」，来自 dynasthai「能够」。同一词根还给出英语 dynamic 与 dynamite。

items.en: The compound thermo- plus dynamics follows the pattern of other nineteenth-century subject names and means literally 'the study of heat-power'.
items.cn: 由 thermo- 加 dynamics 构成的复合词沿用了 19 世纪其他学科名的造词方式，字面意思是「研究热与力的学问」。

items.en: James Thomson is generally credited with the English term in 1849, and Thomson and Kelvin spread it through their work on heat engines. The exact first printing is a detail on which sources differ.
items.cn: 一般认为英语术语由 James Thomson 于 1849 年提出，并经他与开尔文的热机研究传播开来。最早的确切印刷出处各家记载不一，属仅首见年代存疑。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper root and first date): the pre-Greek origin of thermē is unsettled and the earliest citation is not firmly fixed, so neither should be stated as fact.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词根与首见年代）：thermē 在希腊语之前的来源无定论，最早书证也未完全确定，两者都不宜当作定论陈述。

note.en: Group one holds look-alike words that share the Greek thermo- or dynam- element but name different things; group two holds neighbouring sciences with a different scope.
note.cn: 第一组是共享希腊 thermo- 或 dynam- 成分但所指不同的形近词；第二组是范围不同、彼此相邻的学科名。

entries.definition: From Greek dynamis 'power' but with no thermo- element: it describes force, energy or constant change, not the science of heat.
entries.definitionCN: 只共享希腊 dynamis「力」，不含 thermo- 成分：形容力量、活力或不断变化，并非研究热的学科。

entries.definition: The study of forces and motion; thermodynamics is a separate subject that adds heat to the accounting.
entries.definitionCN: 研究力与运动的学科；热力学是另一门学科，在账目里加入了热。

entries.definition: Thermo- plus metron 'measure': an instrument for reading temperature, not a branch of physics.
entries.definitionCN: thermo- 加 metron「测量」：读温度的仪器，不是物理学分支。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning 'relating to heat', built on the same thermē root; it cannot name the discipline.
entries.definitionCN: 由同一 thermē 词根构成的形容词，意为「热的、热量的」，不能用来指这门学科。

entries.definition: The whole science of matter, energy and motion; thermodynamics is one of its branches.
entries.definitionCN: 研究物质、能量与运动的整个学科；热力学只是它的一个分支。

entries.definition: The study of forces and motion without the heat accounting that thermodynamics adds.
entries.definitionCN: 研究力与运动的学问，不含热力学加入的热量账目。

entries.definition: The practice of measuring heat exchanged in a process; it supplies data rather than the general laws.
entries.definitionCN: 测量过程中热交换量的实务；它提供数据，而非普遍定律。

entries.definition: The broad study of energy transformations in physical and chemical systems, of which thermodynamics is the strict heat-and-work core.
entries.definitionCN: 研究物理与化学系统中能量转换的宽泛学问，热力学是其严格处理热与功的核心部分。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Greek morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊语构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: thermo- 'heat' + dynamics 'power': the study of heat becoming power.
normal.cn: thermo-「热」+ dynamics「动力」：研究热如何变成动力的学问。

normal.en: The pair of laws is the backbone: the first keeps the books balanced, the second fixes the direction.
normal.cn: 两条定律是骨架：第一定律让账目平衡，第二定律定下方向。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: laws of thermodynamics, engineering thermodynamics, chemical thermodynamics.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：热力学定律、工程热力学、化学热力学。

normal.en: Shared morphemes appear in thermometer, thermal and dynamic.
normal.cn: 共享的构词成分出现在 thermometer、thermal 与 dynamic 中。

normal.en: The subject name ends in -ics and takes a singular verb, like physics and economics.
normal.cn: 学科名以 -ics 结尾，谓语用单数，与 physics、economics 一样。

abstract.en: Picture a sealed ledger in which every joule entering must be written on the other page as work or heat.
abstract.cn: 想象一本密封的账本，每进一焦耳，就必须在另一页记成功或热。

abstract.en: Picture a hill that a ball can roll down for free but can never roll up without being pushed.
abstract.cn: 想象一个斜坡，球可以自己滚下去，却不可能不被推就滚上来。

abstract.en: Picture a room full of scattered papers that will never gather back into neat stacks by themselves.
abstract.cn: 想象一屋子散落的纸页，永远不会自己重新叠成整齐的几摞。

examples.en: The whole plant is designed around the second law of thermodynamics.
examples.cn: 整座工厂的设计都以热力学第二定律为依据。

examples.en: Her lecture made thermodynamics feel like a branch of bookkeeping.
examples.cn: 她的讲座让热力学听起来像会计学的一个分支。

examples.en: No thermodynamics course can avoid the problem of wasted heat.
examples.cn: 任何热力学课程都绕不开废热的问题。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「热」加「动力」再加学科词尾——研究热如何变成动力的学问，就是热力学

root: 希腊 thermē「热」+ dynamis「力、能力」+ 学科后缀 -ics；19 世纪按科学命名惯例构成，一般认为由 James Thomson 于 1849 年提出英语术语。thermē 在希腊语之前的来源不确定，不作印欧构拟；该词无拉丁语祖传同族词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one line: heat is treated as something that can be booked and moved, from the general science to its two laws, then to engines, reactions, crowds of molecules, a figurative ledger and finally a classroom subject.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一条线索展开：把热当成可以记账、可以搬运的东西，从总学科到两条定律，再到热机、化学反应、分子群体、比喻账本，最后落到课堂上的学科名。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: steam pushing a piston, heat turned into measurable work.
core.cn: 核心意象：蒸汽推动活塞，热被换算成可测量的功。

branches.en: THE TWO LAWS: one keeps the total, the other fixes the direction of change.
branches.cn: 两条定律：一条守住总量，一条定下变化的方向。

branches.en: MACHINES: the laws are applied to boilers, turbines and the ceiling on efficiency.
branches.cn: 机器：定律被用于锅炉、涡轮机与效率上限。

branches.en: REACTIONS: the same accounting is moved from steam to chemical bonds.
branches.cn: 反应：同一套账目从蒸汽搬到化学键上。

branches.en: CROWDS OF MOLECULES: temperature becomes a statistical fact about many particles.
branches.cn: 分子群体：温度成为关于大量粒子的统计事实。

branches.en: LEDGER, NAME AND FIELD: the accounting image spreads to daily effort, then to the course label, and the whole discipline bears that name.
branches.cn: 账本、名称与学科：记账的意象扩展到日常精力，再落到课程名目，整个学科也以此命名。

intro.en: Thermodynamics can be read as three pieces: the combining form thermo-, the root dynam-, and the subject suffix -ics; the same pieces build several everyday English words.
intro.cn: thermodynamics 可以拆成三块：组合成分 thermo-、词根 dynam- 与学科后缀 -ics；这三块还构成若干日常英语词。

latinIntro.en: Both roots are Greek, and Latin has no inherited forms of this compound; the modern Latinized spelling is only a later borrowing for international use, so no Latin entries are listed.
latinIntro.cn: 两个词根都来自希腊语，拉丁语没有这个复合词的祖传形式；现代拉丁化拼写只是后来为国际通用而借用的形式，因此不列拉丁词条。

items.example: A thermometer measures heat with a column of liquid.
items.exampleCN: 温度计用一段液柱测量热度。

items.example: A dynamo turns motion into electric power.
items.exampleCN: 发电机把运动转化为电力。

items.example: Physics and economics both end in the same suffix.
items.exampleCN: physics 与 economics 都以同一后缀结尾。

items.example: The thermodynamic limit caps the efficiency.
items.exampleCN: 热力学极限给效率设了上限。

items.meaning: in terms of heat and work
items.meaningCN: 从热力学角度；在热力学上
items.exampleCN: 这个反应在热力学上是有利的。

items.example: The thermodynamicist modelled the cooling tower.
items.exampleCN: 这位热力学专家对冷却塔做了建模。

items.example: The thermometer on the wall read twenty degrees.
items.exampleCN: 墙上的温度计读数是二十度。

items.meaning: full of force or constant change
items.example: The market stayed dynamic all year.
items.exampleCN: 市场整年都保持活跃变化。

items.example: Thermal gloves keep the fingers warm.
items.exampleCN: 保暖手套让手指保持温暖。

definition_zh: 序言；前言；开场白；铺垫
definition_en: the part that comes before the main text or the main point
core_image: 一队人走在前面开路，真正的队伍还没出现
scene: 他没寒暄，也没铺垫，直接说出结论。 He offered no greeting and no preamble, and gave the conclusion first.
sceneCN: 这里 preamble 指讲话前的开场铺垫（第 3 个义项：讲话开场）；句意为他没有寒暄、也没有铺垫，开口就是结论。

pos.zh: 序言；前言；开场白；铺垫

senses.title: Constitutional preamble
senses.definition: the opening paragraph that states why a constitution exists
senses.definitionCN: 说明宪法为何存在的开篇段落
senses.example: The preamble begins with the words 'We the people'.
senses.exampleCN: 序言以「我们人民」这几个字开头。
senses.why: Here the opening carries legal weight and is quoted in court.
senses.whyCN: 这里开篇承载法律效力，会在法庭上被引用。

senses.title: Treaty preamble
senses.definition: the section that names the parties and the purpose before the articles
senses.definitionCN: 在条款之前点明各方与目的的段落
senses.example: The treaty's preamble listed three reasons and no promises.
senses.exampleCN: 条约序言列了三条理由，没有一条承诺。
senses.why: Diplomacy puts its intentions first so that the rules can follow.
senses.whyCN: 外交把意图放在前面，好让规则随后跟上。

senses.title: Speech opening
senses.definition: the remarks made before the point is reached
senses.definitionCN: 在进入正题之前的几句交代
senses.example: He offered no greeting and no preamble, and gave the conclusion first.
senses.exampleCN: 他没有寒暄也没有铺垫，开口就是结论。
senses.why: In speech the word measures patience rather than law.
senses.whyCN: 在讲话里，这个词衡量的是耐心，不是法律。

senses.title: Legal recital
senses.definition: the statement of facts a document must recite before its operative clauses
senses.definitionCN: 文件在生效条款之前必须陈述的事实
senses.example: The deed's preamble recited the old boundary twice.
senses.exampleCN: 这份契据的前提陈述把旧边界写了两遍。
senses.why: Law requires the story before the command.
senses.whyCN: 法律要求先讲故事，再下命令。

senses.title: Warning prologue
senses.definition: words that prepare a listener for bad news
senses.definitionCN: 为坏消息作准备的几句话
senses.example: His preamble about 'difficult decisions' told the room what was coming.
senses.exampleCN: 他关于「艰难决定」的铺垫让全屋人都知道要出什么。
senses.why: A preamble can soften a blow or announce it.
senses.whyCN: 铺垫可以减轻打击，也可以预告它。

senses.title: Book preface
senses.definition: the few pages in which an author explains the book's aim
senses.definitionCN: 作者用几页说明本书目的的篇幅
senses.example: The preamble thanks four libraries and no readers.
senses.exampleCN: 绪言感谢了四家图书馆，一个读者也没提。
senses.why: Publishing kept the word for the author's own voice.
senses.whyCN: 出版业保留这个词，指作者自己的声音。

senses.title: Empty preamble
senses.definition: a formal opening with nothing behind it
senses.definitionCN: 背后空空的程式化开场
senses.example: The report buried its one fact under a long preamble.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告把唯一的事实埋在一段冗长开场下面。
senses.why: The word turns critical when the opening outgrows the text.
senses.whyCN: 当开场长得超过正文，这个词就变得带批评意味。

senses.title: Any preparation
senses.definition: whatever is said or done to set up what follows
senses.definitionCN: 为使后文成立而先说的话或先做的事
senses.example: The apology was only a preamble to the request.
senses.exampleCN: 那句道歉只是请求之前的铺垫。
senses.why: This is the loosest sense, and the most common in speech.
senses.whyCN: 这是最宽松的义项，也是口语里最常见的。

intro.en: Preamble is a walking word: prae- means before, and ambulare means to walk, so the preamble walks in front.
intro.cn: preamble 是一个「走路」的词：prae- 意为在前，ambulare 意为行走，所以序言是在前面走的那部分。

items.en: Ambulare meant 'to walk', the verb behind amble and ambulance.
items.cn: ambulare 意为「行走」，是 amble 与 ambulance 背后的动词。

items.en: Prae- meant 'before, in front', giving the walking a direction.
items.cn: prae- 意为「在前、在面前」，给行走一个方向。

items.en: Late Latin praeambulum named 'that which goes before', a thing that walks ahead.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 praeambulum 指「走在前面之物」。

items.en: English borrowed preamble first for legal and church documents.
items.cn: 英语最初在法律与教会文书里借入 preamble。

items.en: Later the word escaped the law and came to mean any opening remarks.
items.cn: 后来这个词走出法律，泛指任何开场的话。

note.en: The look-alike group is the walking family; the near-meaning group separates preface, prologue, introduction and foreword.
note.cn: 形近组是「行走」词族；近义组把「前言」「序幕」「引言」与「序文」分开。

entries.definition: several opening sections.
entries.definitionCN: 若干段序言。

entries.definition: belonging to a preamble.
entries.definitionCN: 属于序言的。

entries.definition: to walk at an easy pace.
entries.definitionCN: 以轻松步子走。

entries.definition: able to walk, or moving about.
entries.definitionCN: 能行走的；流动的。

entries.definition: an author's opening note.
entries.definitionCN: 作者的开篇说明。

entries.definition: a scene before a play.
entries.definitionCN: 戏剧正场之前的一幕。

entries.definition: a section that brings the reader in.
entries.definitionCN: 把读者带进来的部分。

entries.definition: a short opening by someone other than the author.
entries.definitionCN: 由作者之外的人写的短序。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a small escort walking ahead of the real procession.
normalIntro.cn: 以下联想留住「一小队人走在真正队伍前面开路」的画面。

normal.en: Preamble holds prae (before) and ambulare (to walk): the part that walks in front.
normal.cn: preamble 里藏着 prae（在前）与 ambulare（行走）：走在前面那部分。

normal.en: Think of a speaker clearing his throat before the one sentence that matters.
normal.cn: 想象一位说话者在关键那句之前先清了清嗓子。

normal.en: Pre-AM-ble: the stress sits on am, the middle of the walk.
normal.cn: pre-AM-ble：重音落在 am，正是行走的中段。

normal.en: Say PREE-am-bl; the first syllable is already ahead of the rest.
normal.cn: 读成 PREE-am-bl，第一音节已经走在其余部分前面。

normal.en: Pair it with without: 'without preamble' is the phrase people use when they want the point.
normal.cn: 把它和 without 配对：说 without preamble，就是想要直接说重点。

abstract.en: A preamble is a promise about what kind of text follows, made before the text exists.
abstract.cn: 序言是在正文出现之前，对「接下来是哪种文本」作出的承诺。

abstract.en: The word is at its best when short and at its worst when it outgrows the thing it introduces.
abstract.cn: 这个词短的时候最好，长得超过它所引的东西时最糟。

abstract.en: Law, diplomacy and apology all use preambles because all three need to prepare a listener.
abstract.cn: 法律、外交与道歉都用铺垫，因为三者都需要先安顿听者。

examples.en: He offered no greeting and no preamble, and gave the conclusion first.
examples.cn: 他没有寒暄也没有铺垫，开口就是结论。

examples.en: Smog is not treated here; the preamble explains why the book is short.
examples.cn: 这里不谈雾霾，序言解释了这本书为何写得短。

examples.en: The apology was only a preamble to the request.
examples.cn: 那句道歉只是请求之前的铺垫。

dict_mnemonic.text: pre（在前）+ amble（走）：走在正文前面的一段，就是「序言、铺垫」。

root: 拉丁语 prae（在前）与 ambulare（行走）合成的晚期拉丁语 praeambulum

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses all walk ahead of something: a constitution, a treaty, a remark, a deed, a warning, a book, an empty formality and an apology.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在某样东西前面行走：宪法、条约、一句话、一份契据、一个警告、一本书、一道空洞程序和一句道歉。

core.en: AN ESCORT WALKING AHEAD OF THE PROCESSION
core.cn: 走在队伍前面的那队人

branches.en: A constitution and a treaty.
branches.cn: 宪法与条约。

branches.en: A speech and a warning before bad news.
branches.cn: 一段讲话与坏消息前的警告。

branches.en: A deed reciting its facts.
branches.cn: 一份陈述事实的契据。

branches.en: A book's own note, and the version that outgrows the book.
branches.cn: 书自己的说明，以及那个长得超过正文的版本。

branches.en: The loosest sense: any preparation at all.
branches.cn: 最宽松的义项：任何事前准备。

intro.en: The ambulare family is about walking: amble is an easy walk, ambulance was a moving hospital, and a preamble walks in front of a text.
intro.cn: ambulare 词族关乎行走：amble 是轻松的走，ambulance 曾是会走的医院，preamble 走在文本前面。

latinIntro.en: Latin prae- gives the direction and ambulare gives the gait; praeambulum is simply 'the thing that walks before'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 prae- 给出方向，ambulare 给出步态；praeambulum 就是「走在前面之物」。

definition_zh: 鸟舍；大型鸟笼；鸟类饲养场
definition_en: a large enclosure or building for keeping birds
core_image: 罩着网顶的大笼子，鸟在里面飞而不出
scene: 鹦鹉扑翅掠过网顶的影子。 The zoo opened a walk-through aviary last spring.
sceneCN: 这里 aviary 指「鸟舍」（第 1 个义项：养鸟的大型圈舍）；句意：动物园去年春天开放了一座可步入式鸟舍。

pos.zh: 鸟舍；大型鸟笼

senses.title: A large enclosure for birds
senses.definition: a big cage, enclosure, or building in which birds are kept
senses.definitionCN: 圈养鸟类的大型笼舍或建筑
senses.example: The flamingos moved to a new aviary by the lake.
senses.exampleCN: 火烈鸟迁入了湖边的新鸟舍。
senses.why: The Latin root is avis, bird: the place named for its dwellers.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根是 avis「鸟」：以住户为场所命名。

senses.title: A domestic bird house
senses.definition: a smaller outdoor cage kept by hobbyists for pet birds
senses.definitionCN: 爱好者在庭院饲养宠物鸟的较小笼舍
senses.example: He built a backyard aviary for his budgies.
senses.exampleCN: 他为虎皮鹦鹉搭了座后院鸟舍。
senses.why: Scale alone separates the hobby shed from the zoo hall.
senses.whyCN: 业余小棚与动物园大馆只是规模之别。

senses.title: A zoo exhibit for flying birds
senses.definition: a zoo building designed so birds can fly free inside
senses.definitionCN: 园内供鸟类自由飞翔的展区建筑
senses.example: The walk-through aviary lets visitors share the airspace.
senses.exampleCN: 可步入式鸟舍让游客与鸟共享同一片空气。
senses.why: Designers inverted the cage: the humans enter the birds' room.
senses.whyCN: 设计者把笼子倒了过来：人走进鸟的房间。

senses.title: A breeding establishment
senses.definition: a facility where birds are bred for conservation or sale
senses.definitionCN: 为保育或出售而繁育鸟类的场所
senses.example: The sanctuary's aviary raises endangered parrots.
senses.exampleCN: 保护区的鸟舍繁育濒危鹦鹉。
senses.why: Keeping became breeding as conservation grew.
senses.whyCN: 随着保育兴起，「养鸟」变成了「繁育鸟」。

senses.title: A quarantine aviary
senses.definition: an enclosure where imported birds are held for inspection
senses.definitionCN: 隔离检疫进口鸟类用的圈舍
senses.example: Imported finches spent a month in the quarantine aviary.
senses.exampleCN: 进口雀鸟在检疫鸟舍待了一个月。
senses.why: Enclosure plus oversight is the aviary idea turned official.
senses.whyCN: 圈舍加监管，正是鸟舍概念的正装版本。

senses.title: Figurative: a noisy gathering
senses.definition: a place or group compared to a cage of chattering birds
senses.definitionCN: 被比作满笼啁啾之鸟的场所或人群
senses.example: The press room was an aviary before the verdict.
senses.exampleCN: 宣判前，记者室像座嘈杂的鸟舍。
senses.why: The bird image carries noise and restless movement.
senses.whyCN: 鸟的意象自带聒噪与躁动。

senses.title: In hawking history, the mews house
senses.definition: in older usage, housing for hawks and other hunting birds
senses.definitionCN: 旧义指饲养鹰隼等猎禽的房舍
senses.example: The manor kept an aviary for the falconer's birds.
senses.exampleCN: 庄园为驯鹰师的猎禽专设鹰舍。
senses.why: Before zoos, keeping birds meant keeping hunting partners.
senses.whyCN: 动物园之前，养鸟即是养狩猎伙伴。

senses.title: In architecture, the bird-room of a house
senses.definition: a glazed room of a country house set aside for birds
senses.definitionCN: 乡间宅邸中专辟给鸟类的玻璃花房式房间
senses.example: The conservatory doubled as the family aviary.
senses.exampleCN: 那间暖房兼作全家的鸟室。
senses.why: Estate architecture folded the aviary into the house itself.
senses.whyCN: 庄园建筑把鸟舍折进了住宅本体。

intro.en: Aviary comes from Latin aviarium, a place for birds, from avis, bird, plus the place-ending -arium; English adopted the word in the sixteenth century.
intro.cn: aviary 出自拉丁语 aviarium「养鸟之所」，由 avis（鸟）+ 表场所的后缀 -arium 构成；英语于 16 世纪采纳该词。

items.en: The bird-root is reconstructed as awi- or h₂ewis, the old word for bird.
items.cn: 「鸟」词根被重构为 awi-/h₂ewis，即古老的「鸟」词。

items.en: avis meant bird and seeded a whole family: avian, aviation, aviator.
items.cn: avis 意为鸟，衍生出一整个词族：avian、aviation、aviator。

items.en: Romans kept aviaria for songbirds and doves in villas and temples.
items.cn: 罗马人在别墅与神庙设 aviaria 饲养鸣禽与鸽。

items.en: The neuter aviarium passed into Romance forms of the bird-place.
items.cn: 中性名词 aviarium 进入罗曼语族的「鸟舍」一词。

items.en: English borrowed aviary in the 1570s-80s for cages and bird-rooms.
items.cn: 英语在 1570 至 1580 年代借入 aviary，指鸟笼与鸟室。

items.en: The great walk-through aviaries of zoos redefined the word in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries.
items.cn: 19、20 世纪动物园的大型步入式鸟舍重新定义了这个词。

note.en: Group one gathers the avis family and a spelling trap; group two gathers homes of animals.
note.cn: 第一组收 avis 词族及拼写陷阱；第二组收动物居所的词。

entries.definition: a place for bees, from apis; one letter turns birds into insects.
entries.definitionCN: 养蜂场，出自 apis「蜂」；一字之差，鸟变虫。

entries.definition: flight and the aircraft industry, from the same avis.
entries.definitionCN: 航空；同出 avis 词根。

entries.definition: adjective, of or relating to birds.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词：鸟类的。

entries.definition: a small barred container for one or a few birds.
entries.definitionCN: 小笼，装一只或少数几只鸟。

entries.definition: a small pen for poultry.
entries.definitionCN: 家禽的小围棚。

entries.definition: the same -ary place-word, for bees.
entries.definitionCN: 同款 -ary 场所词，住户换成蜂。

entries.definition: a collection of wild animals kept for exhibition.
entries.definitionCN: 展出用的异兽 collection；鸟舍可为其一角。

entries.definition: historically, buildings where hawks were kept while molting.
entries.definitionCN: 历史上换羽期圈养鹰隼的房舍。

normalIntro.en: Hang the word on avis, the Latin bird: an aviary is where avis lives.
normalIntro.cn: 把词挂在拉丁语 avis「鸟」上：aviary 就是 avis 住的地方。

normal.en: avis bird plus -ary place: like library from liber, book.
normal.cn: avis 鸟 + -ary 场所：正如 liber 书造出 library。

normal.en: Distinguish apiary, bees, from aviary, birds.
normal.cn: 区分 apiary（养蜂场）与 aviary（鸟舍）。

normal.en: Same family: aviation, aviator, avian all fly on avis.
normal.cn: 同族词 aviation、aviator、avian 都乘 avis 起飞。

normal.en: Plural spelling note: aviary becomes aviaries, y to ies.
normal.cn: 复数拼写：aviary 变 aviaries，y 变 ies。

normal.en: walk-through aviary is the modern zoo phrase.
normal.cn: walk-through aviary 是现代动物园的固定说法。

abstract.en: Look up: net instead of sky, yet still sky-colored light.
abstract.cn: 抬头看：网代替了天空，光线却仍是天光。

abstract.en: An aviary is a sky folded down to human size.
abstract.cn: 鸟舍是折叠到人间的天空。

abstract.en: Hear the whole room ticking with small claws and calls.
abstract.cn: 听整间屋子里小爪与鸣叫的窸窣。

examples.en: Volunteers repaired the storm-torn aviary before dawn.
examples.cn: 志愿者赶在天亮前修好了被风暴撕坏的鸟舍。

examples.en: The parrot slipped out of the aviary and colonized the park.
examples.cn: 那只鹦鹉溜出鸟舍，在公园里安了家。

examples.en: Her garden aviary held a dozen shimmering finches.
examples.cn: 她的花园鸟舍里养着十来只羽色闪亮的雀鸟。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱喂鹅里」——爱喂鸟的鹅住的大笼子，就叫鸟舍

root: 出自拉丁语 aviarium「养鸟之所」，由 avis（鸟）+ 表场所后缀 -arium 构成；avis 词根可追溯至印欧语 awi-「鸟」。英语于 16 世纪后期借入，与 aviation、aviator、avian 同族；19 世纪起随动物园大型鸟舍扩展词义。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses scale the bird-house up and out: the home cage, the zoo hall, the breeding and quarantine sheds, the falconer's mews, and the figurative noisy room.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把「鸟屋」逐级放大：家用笼、动物园大馆、繁育与检疫棚、驯鹰房，以及比喻中喧闹的房间。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: netting stretched where sky should be, birds flying inside it.
core.cn: 核心意象：在天空该在的地方绷起网，鸟在网内飞翔。

branches.en: THE KEEPING SIDE: from home shed to collection.
branches.cn: 饲养一面：从家庭小棚到收藏大笼。

branches.en: THE EXHIBIT SIDE: humans stepping into the birds' air.
branches.cn: 展出一面：人步入鸟的天空。

branches.en: THE OFFICIAL SIDE: breeding programs and quarantine lines.
branches.cn: 公务一面：繁育计划与检疫线。

branches.en: THE OLD SIDE: hawks housed for the hunt.
branches.cn: 古义一面：为狩猎而养的鹰房。

branches.en: THE FIGURATIVE SIDE: chatter and glassed-in rooms.
branches.cn: 比喻一面：聒噪人群与宅内鸟室。

intro.en: Aviary is avis plus -arium, one of Latin's most regular place-endings.
intro.cn: aviary 即 avis 加 -arium，后者是拉丁语最规整的场所后缀之一。

latinIntro.en: Latin -arium built names for where things live or are kept, from aquarium to armamentarium.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 -arium 为「存放、栖居之所」命名，从 aquarium 到 armamentarium 皆是。

definition_zh: 深海的；深渊带的；无底的；深不可测的
definition_en: relating to the deepest part of the ocean or to an abyss, or figuratively meaning unfathomably deep
core_image: 探照灯的光柱在漆黑水里只照出一小片悬浮的白色颗粒，下方仍是没有尽头的黑
scene: 深海的探测器在黑暗里拍到了一只苍白的小虾。 The abyssal zone receives no sunlight at all.
sceneCN: 这里 abyssal 指「属于深海深渊带的」（第 2 个义项：海洋深渊带的）；句意为深渊带完全接收不到阳光。图中可辨识物件：探照灯光柱、悬浮颗粒、苍白的小虾、漆黑水体。

pos.zh: 深海的；深渊带的；无底的；深不可测的

forms.label: 形容词（极糟糕的；深不可测的）

senses.title: Literally bottomless
senses.titleCN: 字面义：无底的、深不见底的
senses.definition: having no measurable bottom; extremely and seemingly endless in depth
senses.definitionCN: 没有可测量的底部；深得看似没有尽头
senses.example: The shaft looked abyssal, a black line cut into the rock.
senses.exampleCN: 那口竖井像无底一般，是岩石上切开的一道黑线。
senses.why: abyssal is simply the adjective of abyss, which comes from Greek abyssos 'bottomless', so the literal meaning is 'having the nature of a bottomless place'.
senses.whyCN: abyssal 就是 abyss 的形容词，而 abyss 来自希腊 abyssos「无底的」，因此字面义是「具有无底之处性质的」。

senses.title: Of the abyssal zone
senses.definition: belonging to the deep ocean zone roughly between four and six thousand metres
senses.definitionCN: 属于大约四千米到六千米深的海洋水层
senses.example: The abyssal zone receives no sunlight at all.
senses.exampleCN: 深渊带完全接收不到阳光。
senses.why: oceanography fixed abyssal as the name of a depth zone, turning a poetic word into a measured label.
senses.whyCN: 海洋学把 abyssal 固定为一个深度带的名称，使这个诗意的词变成可测量的标签。

senses.title: Of the abyssal plain
senses.definition: describing the broad, nearly flat surfaces of the deepest ocean floor
senses.definitionCN: 描述最深洋底上宽阔而近乎平坦的表面
senses.example: Turbidites spread across the abyssal plain after the slope collapsed.
senses.exampleCN: 陆坡崩塌后，浊流沉积铺满深海平原。
senses.why: the plain is the flattest part of the abyss, so the adjective naturally names its landform.
senses.whyCN: 平原是深渊中最平坦的部分，因此这个形容词自然用来指它的地貌。

senses.title: Of deep-sea sediment
senses.definition: describing the fine oozes and clays that accumulate on the deepest bottom
senses.definitionCN: 描述堆积在最深底部上的细软泥与黏土
senses.example: Abyssal sediment accumulates only a few millimetres per thousand years.
senses.exampleCN: 深海沉积物每一千年只堆积几毫米。
senses.why: the sediment is the slow skin of the abyss, so the adjective marks material formed in that setting.
senses.whyCN: 沉积物是深渊缓慢形成的表皮，因此这个形容词标示在该环境中形成的物质。

senses.title: Of deep-sea life
senses.definition: describing organisms that live in the deepest water and on its bottom
senses.definitionCN: 描述生活在最深水体及其底部的生物
senses.example: Abyssal fauna depend on organic matter falling from above.
senses.exampleCN: 深海动物群依赖从上方落下的有机物。
senses.why: life adapted to darkness and pressure is named by the zone it inhabits.
senses.whyCN: 适应黑暗与高压的生命，以其栖息的水层命名。

senses.title: At great ocean depth
senses.definition: occurring at very great depth in the sea, without reference to a strict zone boundary
senses.definitionCN: 发生在海中极深之处，不严格限定于某一水层边界
senses.example: Abyssal currents move cold water slowly toward the equator.
senses.exampleCN: 深层水流把冷水缓慢推向赤道。
senses.why: outside technical writing the adjective simply means 'very deep', which keeps the older literal sense alive.
senses.whyCN: 在技术写作之外，这个形容词只表示「极深的」，使较早的字面义继续存活。

senses.title: Of deep-ocean circulation
senses.definition: describing the slow movement of dense water in the deep ocean
senses.definitionCN: 描述深海中高密度海水的缓慢运动
senses.example: Abyssal circulation carries oxygen to the deepest basins.
senses.exampleCN: 深层环流把氧气带到最深的海盆。
senses.why: physical oceanography uses the adjective for the water mass itself, not only for the bottom.
senses.whyCN: 物理海洋学用这个形容词指水团本身，而不只是底部。

senses.title: Figuratively unfathomable
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：深不可测的、难理解的
senses.definition: so profound or obscure that it cannot be understood or measured
senses.definitionCN: 深奥或晦涩到无法理解或衡量
senses.example: The abyssal silence of the archive unsettled the researcher.
senses.exampleCN: 档案库深不可测的寂静让研究者不安。
senses.why: the adjective keeps the metaphor of depth for anything whose extent cannot be sounded.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词把深度的比喻保留给任何无法测知其范围的事物。

intro.en: Abyssal is the English adjective of abyss, formed with -al on a noun that goes back through Latin abyssus to Greek abyssos 'bottomless'. The oceanographic sense is modern. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: abyssal 是 abyss 的英语形容词，由名词加 -al 构成；该名词经拉丁 abyssus 上溯到希腊 abyssos「无底的」。海洋学义属现代。年代均为约数。

items.en: Abyssos meant 'bottomless', from a- 'not' plus byssos 'bottom'. It described the sea and the underworld before it described any measured zone.
items.cn: abyssos 意为「无底的」，由 a-「不」加 byssos「底」构成。它先描述海与冥府，后来才描述可测量的水层。

items.en: Latin abyssus carried the noun into learned use; a Latin adjective abyssalis is recorded in later technical writing.
items.cn: 拉丁 abyssus 把这个名词带入学术用法；后期的技术写作中可见拉丁形容词 abyssalis。

items.en: English formed abyssal on abyss with the native adjective suffix -al, first in the literal sense 'bottomless'.
items.cn: 英语用 abyss 加本族形容词后缀 -al 构成 abyssal，最初取「无底的」字面义。

items.en: Late nineteenth-century deep-sea expeditions gave abyssal its modern zone sense, fixed in the twentieth century.
items.cn: 十九世纪末的深海考察赋予 abyssal 现代水层义，并在二十世纪固定下来。

items.en: The figurative sense for anything unfathomable grew from the literal depth and remains common in literary prose.
items.cn: 用于任何不可测之物的比喻义由字面深度引申而来，至今在文学散文中常见。

items.en: Source uncertain: the pre-Greek origin of byssos is unsettled, and the exact date when abyssal entered English is given only approximately.
items.cn: 来源不确定：byssos 在希腊语之前的来源未有定论，abyssal 进入英语的确切年代也只能给出约数。

note.en: Group one separates abyssal from the other members of its own family; group two holds depth adjectives from oceanography and general prose.
note.cn: 第一组把 abyssal 与其同族其他成员分开；第二组是海洋学与一般散文中的深度形容词。

entries.definition: The noun names the deep place; abyssal is the adjective that describes something belonging to it.
entries.definitionCN: 名词指深处这个地方；abyssal 是描述属于该处之物的形容词。

entries.definition: Formed on the older abysm, it now means 'very bad' and is not a neutral depth adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 建立在较旧的 abysm 之上，今义为「极糟糕的」，并非中性的深度形容词。

entries.definition: An archaic or poetic noun for an abyss; it is a doublet, not an adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 指深渊的古语或诗歌名词；它是同源变体，并非形容词。

entries.definition: A technical adjective for the water layer above the deepest bottom; abyssal can describe both water and bottom.
entries.definitionCN: 指最深底部上方水层的技术形容词；abyssal 既可描述水体，也可描述底部。

entries.definition: A broad everyday compound for the deep ocean; abyssal is narrower and more technical.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指深海的常用复合词；abyssal 更窄也更技术化。

entries.definition: Of the deepest trenches below six thousand metres; it is deeper than the abyssal zone and named after Hades.
entries.definitionCN: 指六千米以下最深海沟的；比深渊带更深，词源出自冥王哈得斯。

entries.definition: Of the bottom itself, at any depth; abyssal adds the specific depth range.
entries.definitionCN: 指底部本身的，不限深度；abyssal 另加特定的深度范围。

entries.definition: Deep in feeling or thought; it is the general abstract adjective where abyssal is the dramatic metaphor.
entries.definitionCN: 指情感或思想深沉的；它是通用抽象形容词，而 abyssal 是更具戏剧性的比喻。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: abyss + -al: 'having the nature of the abyss'.
normal.cn: abyss + -al：「具有深渊性质的」。

normal.en: The family runs abyss, abyssal, abysmal, abysm, abyssopelagic.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 abyss、abyssal、abysmal、abysm、abyssopelagic。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the science: abyssal zone, abyssal plain, abyssal sediment, abyssal fauna.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出科学用法：深渊带、深海平原、深海沉积物、深海动物群。

normal.en: The zone lies roughly between four and six thousand metres, below the bathyal and above the hadal.
normal.cn: 这一水层大致位于四千米到六千米之间，在次深海带之下、超深渊带之上。

normal.en: The adjective is paired with plain more often than with any other landform.
normal.cn: 这个形容词最常搭配的地貌词是 plain（平原）。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp that lights only one metre of water and leaves the rest black.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯只照亮一米水体，其余全是黑的。

abstract.en: Picture a snowfall that takes a thousand years to make a layer as thick as a coin.
abstract.cn: 想象一场雪下了一千年，才积起一枚硬币厚的层。

abstract.en: Picture a silence so deep that a single sound would travel for hours.
abstract.cn: 想象一种深得让单个声音要走几个小时才能传到的寂静。

examples.en: Abyssal temperatures stay just above freezing.
examples.cn: 深渊带的温度只略高于冰点。

examples.en: The abyssal plain stretched for hundreds of kilometres.
examples.cn: 深海平原延伸数百公里。

examples.en: The novel describes an abyssal loneliness.
examples.cn: 这部小说描写了一种深不可测的孤独。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「abyss（深渊）+ al（形容词）」——属于深渊的 → 深海的、深渊的、深不可测的

root: abyss 加形容词后缀 -al；abyss 来自希腊 abyssos「无底的」= a-（不）+ byssos（底），经拉丁 abyssus 进入英语；byssos 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one adjective: literally bottomless, then the measured deep zone, its plain, its sediment, its life, great depth in general, deep circulation, and finally the figurative sense of anything unfathomable.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个形容词展开：字面「无底」，接着是可测量的深渊带、其平原、其沉积物、其生命、泛指的极深、深层环流，最后是任何不可测之物的比喻义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lamp beam that lights one small patch of black water.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道灯光只照亮黑水中很小的一片。

branches.en: UNMEASURED DEPTH: the literal no-bottom idea and the general 'very deep' use.
branches.cn: 未测的深度：字面的无底与泛指的「极深」。

branches.en: NAMED ZONE: a measured layer with a formal boundary.
branches.cn: 有名水层：具有正式边界、可测量的层。

branches.en: FLAT AND SLOW: the plain and the sediment built by millennia.
branches.cn: 平坦而缓慢：平原与千年堆积的沉积物。

branches.en: LIFE AND WATER: fauna adapted to darkness, and the circulation that feeds it.
branches.cn: 生命与水：适应黑暗的动物群，以及供养它们的环流。

branches.en: METAPHOR: any silence or mystery that cannot be sounded.
branches.cn: 比喻：任何无法测知的寂静或奥秘。

intro.en: Abyssal joins the noun abyss to the adjective suffix -al; the noun itself is a Greek negative compound, so the whole word can be read in three pieces.
intro.cn: abyssal 把名词 abyss 与形容词后缀 -al 连接起来；名词本身是希腊否定复合词，因此整词可分三段读出。

latinIntro.en: Greek abyssos became Latin abyssus and later abyssalis; English keeps abyss and builds abyssal with the native suffix -al.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 abyssos 变为拉丁 abyssus，后来又有 abyssalis；英语保留 abyss，并用本族后缀 -al 构成 abyssal。

items.example: The prefix denies the noun it joins.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀否定所连接的名词。

items.example: The noun names the floor of a deep place.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指深处的底面。

items.example: The crevasse opened into an abyss.
The suffix turns a noun into an adjective of relation.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把名词变成表关系的形容词。

items.meaning: of the abyss or the deep sea
items.example: Abyssal water stays cold all year.

items.meaning: a flat expanse of deep ocean floor
items.meaningCN: 深海洋底的平坦区域；深海平原
items.example: The abyssal plain lay far below the ship.

items.meaning: the deep water layer of the open ocean
items.example: Few species live in the abyssal zone.

items.meaning: a small elevated feature on the deep floor
items.meaningCN: 深海底的小型隆起；深海丘陵
items.exampleCN: 深海丘陵使平原变得崎岖。

definition_zh: 职业人脉的拓展与维系；计算机网络组网；联网与互联
definition_en: the activity of building and keeping relationships with other people, or the technical work of linking computers into a network
core_image: 会议室里，几个人交换名片后又各自引荐朋友，人与人的关系像线一样一条条接上，越接越密
scene: 招聘会大厅里，一位求职者主动与几家企业代表交谈，交换名片并记下联系方式。 Good networking turns strangers into useful contacts.
sceneCN: 这里指主动与人交往、建立并维护职业关系网（第 1 个义项：职业人脉的拓展与维系）；句意：良好的人脉经营能把陌生人变成有用的联系人。

pos.zh: 人脉拓展；组网；联网

derivatives.zh: 由表示「网」的名词与表示「劳作」的名词复合，义为「网络；建立网络」
由「建立网络」的动词加表示已然的词尾构成，义为「已联网的」
由该动词加表示施动者的词尾构成，义为「善于经营人脉的人」
古英语中表示「网」的名词，是复合词的前半部分
古英语中表示「劳作、工作」的名词，是复合词的后半部分

senses.title: Building a circle of useful contacts
senses.titleCN: 经营有用的联系人圈子
senses.definition: the activity of meeting people and keeping in touch so that they can help one another in work
senses.definitionCN: 主动结识他人并保持联络，使彼此在工作中互帮互助的活动
senses.example: She spent the evening networking with investors and engineers.
senses.exampleCN: 她整晚都在与投资人和工程师们建立联系。
senses.why: The action ending turns the noun for a linked group into the activity of making such links, and the links are people rather than wires.
senses.whyCN: 表示动作的词尾把「相互连接的群体」这一名词变成「建立这种连接」的活动，而这里被连接的是人而不是线缆。

senses.title: Linking computers into a system
senses.definition: the technical work of connecting computers and devices so that they can exchange data
senses.definitionCN: 把计算机与设备连接起来、使它们能够交换数据的技术工作
senses.example: Computer networking is the first course in the department.
senses.exampleCN: 计算机网络组网是该系的第一门课程。
senses.why: The same ending applies to machines: the noun names the work of building a network of linked devices.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词尾也用于机器：这个名词指把设备连成一个网络的工作。

senses.title: The state of being linked
senses.definition: the condition in which separate machines or people are already connected and can reach one another
senses.definitionCN: 彼此分离的机器或人已经接通、能够相互访问的状态
senses.example: Good networking keeps every office in touch with the head office.
senses.exampleCN: 良好的联网让每个办公室都能与总部保持联络。
senses.why: Once the links exist, the noun can name the resulting condition rather than the work that created it.
senses.whyCN: 连接一旦存在，这个名词就可以指由此形成的状态，而不只是创建它的工作。

senses.title: Cooperation between organizations
senses.definition: the forming of working relationships between organizations that share information or resources
senses.definitionCN: 彼此共享信息或资源的机构之间建立工作关系
senses.example: Networking between the two hospitals shortened the waiting list.
senses.exampleCN: 两家医院之间的协作联结缩短了等候名单。
senses.why: The people being linked can also be institutions, so the word extends from personal contacts to organized cooperation.
senses.whyCN: 被连接的对象也可以是机构，因此这个词从个人交往扩展到有组织的合作。

senses.title: Keeping a relationship alive
senses.definition: the ongoing effort to stay in contact with people already known rather than only meeting new ones
senses.definitionCN: 与已经认识的人保持联系、而不只是结识新人的持续努力
senses.example: Networking is mostly follow-up, not the first handshake.
senses.exampleCN: 人脉经营多半靠后续跟进，而不是第一次握手。
senses.why: The action ending marks an ongoing process, so the word covers maintenance as much as first contact.
senses.whyCN: 表示动作的词尾标记一个持续过程，因此这个词既指初次接触，也指关系维护。

senses.title: Interacting on social platforms
senses.definition: the use of online platforms to build and maintain contacts
senses.definitionCN: 借助在线平台建立并维持联系人关系
senses.example: Social networking moved most of her contacts online.
senses.exampleCN: 社交平台活动把她的大部分联系人转到了线上。
senses.why: When the links run through websites, the same activity is named after its medium, giving the phrase social networking.
senses.whyCN: 当连接通过网站进行时，同一活动便以其媒介命名，于是有了「社交网络活动」这一说法。

senses.title: Shared broadcasting across stations
senses.definition: the arrangement in which several stations carry the same programme at the same time
senses.definitionCN: 多家台站在同一时间播出同一节目的安排
senses.example: The three stations are networking the evening news.
senses.exampleCN: 这三家台站正在联播晚间新闻。
senses.why: A broadcasting network is a set of linked stations, so its action ending name means putting a programme across that set.
senses.whyCN: 广播网络就是一组相互连接的台站，因此加动作词尾后指把节目送到这组台站上。

senses.title: Forming a mesh-like structure
senses.definition: the forming of a structure whose parts cross and connect like the threads of a net
senses.definitionCN: 各部分交叉相接、形似网线的结构的形成
senses.example: The roots are networking through the soil in every direction.
senses.exampleCN: 根系正朝各个方向在土壤中结网延伸。
senses.why: The oldest sense of network is a mesh of cords, so the ending can still describe the making of any net-like pattern.
senses.whyCN: 网络最古老的意义就是绳线结成的网，因此这个词尾仍能描述任何网状图案的形成。

intro.en: Networking joins two Old English nouns, net and work, and adds the action ending -ing; the modern senses grew from a literal mesh to linked people and machines.
intro.cn: 这个词由两个古英语名词「网」与「劳作」复合，再加表示动作的词尾构成；现代各义项从字面的网扩展到相互连接的人与机器。

items.en: Net named a mesh of cords used for catching or carrying, and the word has stayed in English for more than a thousand years.
items.cn: 「网」原指用绳索编成、用于捕捉或承载的网状物，这个词在英语中已存续一千多年。

items.en: Work meant labour or a piece of work, and it still supplies the second half of many compounds.
items.cn: 「劳作」原指劳动或一件工作，至今仍是许多复合词的后半部分。

items.en: Network first appears as a noun for a net-like arrangement of threads or pipes, keeping the literal picture of interwoven parts.
items.cn: 复合词最初指绳线或管道交织成的网状结构，保留了「相互编织」的字面画面。

items.en: Railways, telegraph lines and social groups were all called networks because their parts were linked like a mesh.
items.cn: 铁路、电报线路与社交群体都被称为网络，因为它们的组成部分像网一样相互连接。

items.en: As computers were joined into networks, the action ending produced networking for both the engineering work and the human activity of making contacts.
items.cn: 随着计算机被连成网络，表示动作的词尾造出了这个词，既指工程上的组网工作，也指人建立联系的活动。

items.en: The compound is transparent, yet the first recorded date of the career sense is only approximate; the pre-Germanic root of net remains a proposal rather than an established form.
items.cn: 复合词的构词清楚，但职业人脉义项的首见年代只是约数；「网」在日耳曼语之前的词根仍只是假说，并未确证。

note.en: The first group shares the net stem; the second group names neighbouring ways of linking people or systems.
note.cn: 第一组共享「网」这一词干；第二组是连接人或系统的相邻说法。

entries.definition: The linked group itself; networking is the activity of building or using it.
entries.definitionCN: 指相互连接的那个群体本身；而目标词指建立或使用它的活动。

entries.definition: Already connected into a network; it describes the result rather than the work.
entries.definitionCN: 已经接入网络的；描述结果而不是过程。

entries.definition: A person who is skilled at meeting people and keeping useful contacts.
entries.definitionCN: 擅长结识他人并维持有用联系人的人。

entries.definition: The mesh or the network itself, a clipped and informal word.
entries.definitionCN: 指网或网络本身，是简短而口语化的说法。

entries.definition: To link systems to each other; it stresses the technical link between networks rather than social contact.
entries.definitionCN: 把系统彼此连接；强调网络之间的技术连接，而非人际交往。

entries.definition: A working relationship between groups; it stresses coordination rather than personal contacts.
entries.definitionCN: 团体之间的工作关系；强调协调配合，而非私人交往。

entries.definition: Joint work toward a shared aim; broader than networking, which only builds the links.
entries.definitionCN: 为共同目标而合作；比目标词更宽，目标词只负责建立连接。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes and real fixed terms, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分与真实固定搭配，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Net plus work: the word literally says working on a net of links.
normal.cn: 「网」加「工作」：字面就是在一张关系网上做功课。

normal.en: The family runs network, networked, networker and networking.
normal.cn: 同族词包括网络、已联网的、善经营人脉者与目标词本身。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the social side: networking event, business networking, networking skills.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出社交一面：人脉活动、商务人脉拓展、社交联络能力。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the technical side: computer networking, networking cable.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出技术一面：计算机网络组网、网络连接线缆。

normal.en: A mesh of cords is the oldest picture: threads crossing and holding one another.
normal.cn: 绳线结成的网是最古老的画面：线相互交叉又相互固定。

abstract.en: Picture a spider web in which every strand also carries a name card.
abstract.cn: 想象一张蛛网，每根丝上都挂着一张名片。

abstract.en: Picture a rope bridge whose every plank is held by two separate knots.
abstract.cn: 想象一座绳桥，每块木板都由两个独立的结固定。

abstract.en: Picture a choir where each singer knows two others by name and can reach them in a word.
abstract.cn: 想象一个合唱队，每位成员都认识另外两位并能一句话找到他们。

examples.en: Good networking often begins with a genuine question rather than a sales pitch.
examples.cn: 良好的人脉经营往往从一个真诚的问题开始，而不是推销话术。

examples.en: The lab offers a course in networking for second-year students.
examples.cn: 实验室为二年级学生开设了一门组网课程。

examples.en: After the conference she kept networking by email every month.
examples.cn: 会议之后她每月都用邮件继续维系人脉。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「网」加「工作」——在网上做功课，既组网也经营人脉

root: 英语「网」与「劳作」复合，再加表示动作的名词词尾；更早的日耳曼语来源存疑。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one gesture: parts get linked. The parts may be people, computers, organizations, broadcast stations or the threads of a mesh.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一个动作：把部分连接起来。这些部分可以是人、计算机、机构、广播台站，也可以是网线的股股丝线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: threads crossing and holding one another, then people and machines linked in the same pattern.
core.cn: 核心意象：丝线相互交叉、彼此固定，随后人与机器以同样的方式被连接起来。

branches.en: THE SOCIAL CORE: meeting people and keeping contact, which is the sense most learners meet first.
branches.cn: 社交核心：结识他人并保持联系，这是学习者最先遇到的义项。

branches.en: THE MACHINE CORE: linking computers and devices so data can travel between them.
branches.cn: 机器核心：把计算机与设备连起来，让数据能在其间传输。

branches.en: WHAT THE LINKS PRODUCE: a connected condition for offices, and organized cooperation between institutions.
branches.cn: 连接带来的结果：办公室处于联网状态，机构之间形成有组织的合作。

branches.en: HOW THE LINKS ARE KEPT: steady follow-up, and the online platforms that now carry most of it.
branches.cn: 连接如何维持：持续的跟进，以及如今承载大部分联络的在线平台。

branches.en: THE PATTERN ITSELF: stations sharing one programme, and any structure that spreads like a net.
branches.cn: 图案本身：台站共享同一节目，以及任何像网一样铺开的结构。

intro.en: Networking is an English compound with a productive action ending; its parts are native English rather than Latin.
intro.cn: 这个词是英语复合词，带一个能产的表示动作的词尾；各部分来自英语本族语，而非拉丁语。

latinIntro.en: No Latin root stands behind this compound, so the Latin entry list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这个复合词背后没有拉丁词根，因此拉丁词条列表留空。

items.example: The first half of the compound is the old noun for a net.
items.exampleCN: 复合词的前半是表示「网」的古名词。

items.example: The second half names the activity done on the net.
items.exampleCN: 后半指在这张网上进行的活动。

items.meaningCN: 相互连接的群体或系统
items.example: The linked group itself is a network.
items.exampleCN: 相互连接的群体本身就叫网络。

items.example: The ending turns the linked group into the work of linking.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把「连接的群体」变成「建立连接」的工作。

items.example: Networking is the name of that activity.
items.exampleCN: 目标词就是这种活动的名称。

items.example: A networked office already has its links in place.
items.exampleCN: 已联网的办公室已经把连接建好了。

items.meaning: a person who does the action
items.example: A networker is a person who builds contacts.
items.exampleCN: 善经营人脉者就是建立联系人的人。

items.example: The networked devices share one address space.
items.exampleCN: 已联网的设备共享同一个地址空间。

definition_zh: 科学进步；科学进展；科学上的突破；（整体的）科学知识推进
definition_en: progress in scientific knowledge, or a specific step forward such as a discovery or a better method
core_image: 一支温度计的刻度被往前推了一格，旁边旧的那一格还留着淡痕
scene: 显微镜改良之后，医生第一次看清了细胞里那些细小的结构。 The microscope was a scientific advancement that changed medicine within a generation.
sceneCN: 这里指科学上的具体进步或突破（第 2 个义项：一项科学突破）；句意为显微镜是一项在一代人之内改变了医学的科学进步。场景图取象：温度计的刻度被往前推了一格，旧痕仍在。

pos.zh: 科学进步；科学进展（不可数）
一项科学突破；一项具体进展（可数）
（整体的）科学知识推进

derivatives.zh: 科学（出自拉丁语「知识」一词，从「知道」转为系统化的知识）
科学的（加表示「与……有关」的形容词后缀）
科学家（加表示「从事者」的名词后缀）
推进；前进；进展（出自法语「向前」一词，由拉丁语「从前面」而来）
推进；进步；晋升（加表示「行为、结果」的名词后缀）
先进的；高级的（过去分词转形容词，指已经走在前头）

senses.title: Progress of knowledge
senses.definition: the gradual growth of scientific understanding over time
senses.definitionCN: 科学理解随时间逐步增长
senses.example: Scientific advancement depends on instruments as much as on ideas.
senses.exampleCN: 科学进步既靠想法，也靠仪器。
senses.why: The word for going forward is applied to knowledge itself, which is imagined as moving ahead.
senses.whyCN: 表示向前的词被用到了知识上，知识于是被想象成在往前走。

senses.title: A specific breakthrough
senses.definition: one identifiable step forward, such as a discovery, a method or a device
senses.definitionCN: 可指认的一步前进，如一项发现、一种方法或一件器械
senses.example: The microscope was a scientific advancement that changed medicine within a generation.
senses.exampleCN: 显微镜是一项在一代人之内改变了医学的科学进步。
senses.why: Big progress is counted in units, and each unit needs a name it can be pointed at.
senses.whyCN: 大的进步按件来数，每一件都需要一个能指认的名字。

senses.title: Cumulative growth
senses.definition: the accumulation of reliable findings that later work can build on
senses.definitionCN: 可靠发现不断积累，后来的工作可以接着往上建
senses.example: Scientific advancement is cumulative, even when it looks sudden.
senses.exampleCN: 科学进步是累积的，即使看起来像是突然发生。
senses.why: New work stands on published work, so progress is a pile rather than a leap.
senses.whyCN: 新工作站在已发表的工作上，因此进步是一堆而不是一跳。

senses.title: Advance that becomes technology
senses.definition: scientific progress that is taken up in tools, medicine or industry
senses.definitionCN: 被工具、医学或工业吸收的科学进展
senses.example: The sequencing method was a scientific advancement that soon became a clinic test.
senses.exampleCN: 这种测序方法是一项科学进步，很快就成了临床检测。
senses.why: The public usually meets science through its devices, so the phrase often means applied progress.
senses.whyCN: 公众通常经由器械遇见科学，所以这一说法常指应用上的进展。

senses.title: A better method
senses.definition: an improvement in how science is done, such as a new control or a new statistic
senses.definitionCN: 做科学的方式得到改进，如新的对照设计或新的统计方法
senses.example: Randomised trials were a quiet scientific advancement with vast effects.
senses.exampleCN: 随机对照试验是一项安静的科学进步，影响却极大。
senses.why: Methods are invisible in the result but decide whether the result can be trusted.
senses.whyCN: 方法在结果里看不见，却决定结果是否可信。

senses.title: Institutional progress
senses.definition: growth in the institutions, funding or training that support research
senses.definitionCN: 支撑研究的机构、经费或人才培养的增长
senses.example: The new laboratory was called an advancement for the whole region.
senses.exampleCN: 这座新实验室被称为整个地区的一大进步。
senses.why: Institutions speak of advancement when they mean capacity, not a single discovery.
senses.whyCN: 机构说进步时，往往指能力，而不是某一项发现。

senses.title: A claim to be judged
senses.definition: a public claim that something new is progress, which still has to be assessed
senses.definitionCN: 公开宣称某项新事物是进步，但仍需评估
senses.example: Not every scientific advancement announced in a press release survives review.
senses.exampleCN: 并非每个在新闻稿里宣告的科学进步都能挺过评审。
senses.why: The phrase is also used in publicity, and calling something an advancement does not make it one.
senses.whyCN: 这一说法也用于宣传，把一件事称为进步并不等于它真是进步。

senses.title: Progress with a cost
senses.definition: scientific progress considered together with its risks, costs or unequal benefits
senses.definitionCN: 连同风险、代价或分配不均一并考虑的科学进展
senses.example: Every scientific advancement brings a question about who will control it.
senses.exampleCN: 每一项科学进步都会带来一个问题：由谁掌控。
senses.why: The word advance assumes a direction, and critics ask forward for whom.
senses.whyCN: 「前进」一词预设了方向，批评者便问：这是替谁往前。

intro.en: The phrase joins Latin scientia 'knowledge' with French avancement, from Latin abante 'from before'. Both halves are clear; the compound is a modern label for progress.
intro.cn: 这个短语把拉丁语 scientia「知识」与法语 avancement 合在一起，后者出自拉丁语 abante「从前面」。两半来源清楚，这个复合词是现代的进步标签。

items.en: Scire meant to know, and its present participle scientia named knowledge or a body of knowing.
items.cn: scire 意为知道，其现在分词 scientia 指知识或一整套所知。

items.en: Latin scientia covered knowledge in general before English narrowed it to organised, testable knowledge.
items.cn: 拉丁语 scientia 泛指知识，英语后来把它收窄为有组织、可检验的知识。

items.en: Latin abante meant from before or in front, and French built avancer, to move forward, on it.
items.cn: 拉丁语 abante 意为从前面、在前方，法语据此造出 avancer「向前移动」。

items.en: English took advancement in the fifteenth century for promotion and for forward movement in general.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入 advancement，指晋升，也泛指向前推进。

items.en: The adjective scientific appeared in the seventeenth century, when the word science acquired its modern, method-bound sense.
items.cn: 形容词 scientific 出现在十七世纪，当时 science 获得现代那种受方法约束的含义。

items.en: The phrase scientific advancement became common in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries, as progress became a public expectation.
items.cn: 十九与二十世纪，这一短语变得常见，因为进步成了一种公共期待。

note.en: The first group shares one of the two roots or looks close; the second group holds the words used for progress that are not quite the same claim.
note.cn: 第一组或共享两个词根之一，或字形相近；第二组是表示进展但并不等同的说法。

entries.definition: The organised body of knowledge itself, not a step within it.
entries.definitionCN: 有组织的知识本身，而非其中的一步。

entries.definition: The adjective for method, attitude or knowledge of that kind.
entries.definitionCN: 指这类方法、态度或知识的形容词。

entries.definition: To move forward, or a forward step, the verb and noun inside the phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 向前移动或向前一步，是词组里的动词与名词。

entries.definition: Far along in development, describing a state rather than an act.
entries.definitionCN: 发展程度靠前，描述状态而非动作。

entries.definition: A benefit; it looks like advance but comes from a phrase meaning before the front.
entries.definitionCN: 好处；字形近似，却出自意为「在前方」的词组变异。

entries.definition: A sudden decisive advance, sharper and more dramatic than progress.
entries.definitionCN: 突然而决定性的推进，比一般进步更锋利、更戏剧化。

entries.definition: Finding something that already existed, which may or may not be progress.
entries.definitionCN: 发现本已存在之物，未必构成进步。

entries.definition: A new product or practice put to use, closer to application than to knowledge.
entries.definitionCN: 投入应用的新产品、新做法，更近应用而非知识。

entries.definition: General forward movement, which need not be scientific or cumulative.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指向前推进，未必是科学的或累积的。

entries.definition: Progress in tools and technique, the usual partner or rival of the scientific kind.
entries.definitionCN: 工具与技艺上的进展，常与科学进步并列或相争。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real knowing and forward roots, the real family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的「知道」与「向前」词根、真实词族与真实固定搭配。

normal.en: Scire is to know and abante is in front, so scientific advancement is knowledge moving forward.
normal.cn: 前者是知道，后者是在前，合起来就是知识向前走。

normal.en: The family runs science, scientific, scientist, advance, advancement and advanced.
normal.cn: 同族词有 science、scientific、scientist、advance、advancement 与 advanced。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: a major scientific advancement, the pace of scientific advancement, scientific and technological advancement.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出用法：一项重大科学进步、科学进步的速度、科学与技术进步。

normal.en: The plural counts individual steps; the singular names the whole movement.
normal.cn: 复数数的是具体步伐，单数指整个进程。

normal.en: Advancement is not the same as advantage, which is only a benefit.
normal.cn: 进步不同于优势，后者只是好处。

abstract.en: Scientific advancement enlarges what can be done before it settles what should be done.
abstract.cn: 科学进步先扩大能做的事，然后才轮到该做的事。

abstract.en: The word assumes a direction; the argument is always about who is being carried forward.
abstract.cn: 这个词预设了方向，争论总在于谁被带着向前。

abstract.en: An advancement is measured backwards, by what later work can no longer imagine doing without.
abstract.cn: 进步是倒着量的，量的是后来的工作再也无法想象缺少什么。

examples.en: Clean water was a scientific advancement that saved more lives than any drug.
examples.cn: 洁净水是一项科学进步，救的命比任何药物都多。

examples.en: Scientific advancement slowed when the funding was cut.
examples.cn: 经费被削减后，科学进步慢了下来。

examples.en: The committee asked whether the device was a real scientific advancement.
examples.cn: 委员会追问这件装置是否真是科学上的进步。

dict_mnemonic.text: 记作「知识向前走一格」——刻度又推进了一格：科学进步

root: scientific（拉丁语 scientia「知识」← scire「知道」＋形容词词尾）＋ advancement（法语 avancement ← 拉丁语 abante「从前、在前」）。science 在十七世纪收窄为受方法约束的知识体系，这一复合短语在十九、二十世纪成为公共用语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one forward movement: the growth of understanding, a specific breakthrough, cumulative findings, applied technology, better method, institutional capacity, a claim still to be judged, and progress weighed with its costs.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着同一次向前：理解的生长、一项具体突破、累积的发现、转入应用的技术、更好的方法、机构能力、仍待评判的宣称，以及连同代价一并称量的进步。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gauge whose mark has been pushed one notch forward, the old notch still faintly visible.
core.cn: 核心意象：刻度被往前推了一格，旧的一格还留着淡痕。

branches.en: THE LONG MOVEMENT: understanding grows, and each reliable finding lets the next stand on it.
branches.cn: 漫长的移动：理解在生长，每个可靠发现都让下一个站上去。

branches.en: THE SINGLE STEP: a device or a better method that can be pointed at and dated.
branches.cn: 单独的一步：能指认、能定年的一件器械或一种更好的方法。

branches.en: THE APPLIED AND THE INSTITUTIONAL: progress taken up by clinics and industry, or by laboratories and funding.
branches.cn: 应用与制度：被诊所与工业吸收的进展，或被实验室与经费吸收的进展。

branches.en: THE CLAIM: a press release's word for progress, which review has not yet settled.
branches.cn: 宣称：新闻稿里对进步的称呼，评审尚未定论。

branches.en: THE COST: the same step seen with its risks and its unequal benefits.
branches.cn: 代价：同一步伐连同风险与分配不均一起看。

intro.en: The phrase combines a Latin word of knowing with a French word of moving forward, and both halves support large families.
intro.cn: 这个短语把拉丁的「知道」与法语的「向前」合在一起，两半都支撑着大词族。

latinIntro.en: Scientia and abante are the sources behind scientific and advancement.
latinIntro.cn: scientia 与 abante 是 scientific 与 advancement 背后的来源。

items.example: The phrase can mean one step or the whole movement.
items.exampleCN: 这个短语可指一步，也可指整个进程。

items.example: It supplies the present participle behind scientia.
items.exampleCN: 它提供 scientia 背后的现在分词。

items.example: English narrowed it to organised, testable knowledge.
items.exampleCN: 英语把它收窄为有组织、可检验的知识。

items.example: It appears in scientific and specific.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在 scientific 与 specific 中。

items.example: It builds scientist, the person who knows by method.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 scientist，指以方法求知的人。

items.example: The verb supplies the movement in advancement.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供 advancement 中的移动。

items.example: It builds advancement, agreement and measurement.
items.exampleCN: 它构成进步、一致与测量等词。

items.example: It appears in advanced and in advance.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在 advanced 与 advance 中。

latinEntries.example: The noun gives the first half of the phrase.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 这个名词提供该短语的前半部分。

latinEntries.structure: Latin verb scire (sci-, scitum; to know)
latinEntries.example: The verb is the oldest element behind the phrase.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 这个动词是该短语背后最古老的成分。

latinEntries.example: Late Latin abante means from before, in front.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 晚期拉丁语 abante 意为从前、在前。
